<div><tool-call id="toolu_01CDQVVginMKGuf8qYe3ku9M"><script type="application/json">{"version":2,"name":"read","input":{"file_path":"/Users/robertdavies/Dropbox/teaching-critical-thinking/sampling-distributions.R"},"caption":"sampling-distributions.R","captionLink":"sampling-distributions.R"}</script></tool-call></div>

<div><tool-result call-id="toolu_01P9DVNsiwRvuxTdjZbzfm2g"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 8.8KB, 214 lines, showing lines 1-214]\n1\t#' =======================================...[truncated, total 9836 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 8.8KB, 214 lines, showing lines 1-214]\n#' ============================================================\n#' testing-sequence.R\n#'\n#' Extends person-grid.R with a \"person at a computer\" composite icon,\n#' for the narrative sequence: one person doing the task -> two people\n#' doing the task -> a whole sample doing the task (grid, no scores\n#' shown). Same silhouette/age/disability/colour parametrization as\n#' person-grid.R carries straight over, including person-grid.R's two\n#' fill modes: \"diversity\" (sampled skin tones) or \"value\" (continuous\n#' diverging scale driven by a numeric score/effect per icon).\n#'\n#' The screen is sized and positioned to face the head (vertically\n#' centred on it, at a fixed horizontal offset) so the icon reads as\n#' \"a person looking at a screen\" rather than two unrelated shapes.\n#'\n#' Requires person-grid.R to be sourced first (same folder).\n#'\n#' Quarto usage:\n#'   ```{r}\n#'   source(\"person-grid.R\")\n#'   source(\"testing-sequence.R\")\n#'   testing_icons(n = 1, scores = 27)$plot\n#'   testing_icons(n = 2, scores = c(31, 24))$plot\n#'   testing_icons(n = 30, seed = 7)$plot   # no `scores` -> sample, no labels\n#'   # colour-by-score instead of sampled diversity:\n#'   testing_icons(n = 6, mode = \"value\", value = c(-2, -1, 0, 0.5, 1, 2))$plot\n#'   ```\n#' ============================================================\n\nlibrary(ggplot2)\n\n# ---- monitor/computer geometry -------------------------------------------\n\n#' Screen geometry in the same local coordinate frame as person_parts()\n#' (head centred at x = 0, y = 1.62), so it can be positioned relative\n#' to the head and scaled/offset identically to the person. Sized and\n#' vertically centred on the head so the pair reads as \"looking at a\n#' screen\" rather than a monitor floating near the feet.\nmonitor_parts \u003c- function(scale = 1, ox = 0, oy = 0,\n                           center_y = 1.62, x_offset = 0.80) {\n  bezel_hw \u003c- 0.40\n  bezel_hh \u003c- 0.34\n  inset \u003c- 0.05\n  neck_h \u003c- 0.10\n  neck_hw \u003c- 0.04\n  base_hw \u003c- 0.22\n  base_h \u003c- 0.05\n\n  bezel_top \u003c- center_y + bezel_hh\n  bezel_bottom \u003c- center_y - bezel_hh\n  neck_top \u003c- bezel_bottom\n  neck_bottom \u003c- neck_top - neck_h\n  base_top \u003c- neck_bottom\n  base_bottom \u003c- base_top - base_h\n\n  parts \u003c- list(\n    bezel  = data.frame(x = x_offset + c(-bezel_hw, bezel_hw, bezel_hw, -bezel_hw),\n                         y = c(bezel_top, bezel_top, bezel_bottom, bezel_bottom)),\n    screen = data.frame(x = x_offset + c(-bezel_hw + inset, bezel_hw - inset,\n                                          bezel_hw - inset, -bezel_hw + inset),\n                         y = c(bezel_top - inset, bezel_top - inset,\n                               bezel_bottom + inset, bezel_bottom + inset)),\n    # inverted-T stand: narrow neck down to a wider foot\n    neck   = data.frame(x = x_offset + c(-neck_hw, neck_hw, neck_hw, -neck_hw),\n                         y = c(neck_top, neck_top, neck_bottom, neck_bottom)),\n    base   = data.frame(x = x_offset + c(-base_hw, base_hw, base_hw, -base_hw),\n                         y = c(base_top, base_top, base_bottom, base_bottom))\n  )\n  out \u003c- lapply(names(parts), function(nm) {\n    p \u003c- parts[[nm]]\n    data.frame(part = nm, x = ox + scale * p$x, y = oy + scale * p$y)\n  })\n  do.call(rbind, out)\n}\n\n#' One person + screen, as a single composite polygon set with a `role`\n#' column (\"person\" vs \"monitor\") so they can be filled differently.\nperson_at_computer \u003c- function(kind = \"A\", age = \"adult\", disabled = FALSE,\n                                scale = 1, ox = 0, oy = 0,\n                                person_color = \"#3B6EA5\",\n                                screen_color = \"#CFE8FF\",\n                                frame_color = \"#555555\") {\n  p \u003c- person_parts(kind, age, disabled, scale, ox, oy)\n  p$role \u003c- \"person\"\n  p$fill \u003c- person_color\n\n  m \u003c- monitor_parts(scale = scale, ox = ox, oy = oy)\n  m$role \u003c- \"monitor\"\n  m$fill \u003c- ifelse(m$part == \"screen\", screen_color, frame_color)\n\n  rbind(p, m)\n}\n\n# ---- main sequence function -----------------------------------------------\n\n#' Draw n copies of \"person at computer\".\n#'\n#' @param n        how many icons (1 = single participant, 2 = a pair,\n#'                 larger = a sample).\n#' @param scores   optional numeric vector of length n; if supplied, each\n#'                 icon gets an \"x = \u003cscore>\" label underneath (used for\n#'                 the n = 1 and n = 2 steps). Leave NULL for the sample\n#'                 grid step, where individual scores aren't shown.\n#' @param ncol     icons per row; default is n itself for n \u003c= 4, else\n#'                 a compact grid.\n#' @param comp_kind, comp_age, disabled_prop, seed: same composition\n#'                 controls as person_grid().\n#' @param mode     \"diversity\" (default; sampled skin-tone fill, as\n#'                 before) or \"value\" (continuous diverging fill driven\n#'                 by `value`, e.g. to colour icons by score/effect).\n#' @param skin_tones hex colours to sample from when mode = \"diversity\".\n#' @param value    numeric vector of length n; required when\n#'                 mode = \"value\". 0 = the null/reference point (see\n#'                 `diverging_colors()` in person-grid.R).\n#' @return list(plot = ggplot object, data = polygon data frame)\ntesting_icons \u003c- function(n, scores = NULL, ncol = NULL,\n                           comp_kind = c(A = 0.45, B = 0.45, N = 0.10),\n                           comp_age = c(adult = 1.0),\n                           disabled_prop = 0,\n                           mode = c(\"diversity\", \"value\"),\n                           skin_tones = c(\"#4A3728\", \"#7A5230\", \"#B07A4E\",\n                                          \"#D9A066\", \"#F0C892\", \"#F5E1C8\"),\n                           value = NULL,\n                           seed = 1, dx = 1.9, dy = 2.5) {\n  mode \u003c- match.arg(mode)\n  if (!is.null(scores)) stopifnot(length(scores) == n)\n  if (is.null(ncol)) ncol \u003c- if (n \u003c= 4) n else min(6, ceiling(sqrt(n)))\n  nrow_ \u003c- ceiling(n / ncol)\n\n  kinds \u003c- sample_counts(n, comp_kind, seed)\n  ages \u003c- sample_counts(n, comp_age, seed + 1)\n  disabled \u003c- sample_counts(n, c(yes = disabled_prop, no = 1 - disabled_prop), seed + 2) == \"yes\"\n\n  if (mode == \"diversity\") {\n    set.seed(seed + 3)\n    colors \u003c- sample(skin_tones, n, replace = TRUE)\n  } else {\n    stopifnot(\"`value` must be supplied and length n when mode = 'value'\" =\n                !is.null(value) && length(value) == n)\n    colors \u003c- diverging_colors(value)\n  }\n\n  polys \u003c- vector(\"list\", n)\n  labels \u003c- vector(\"list\", n)\n  for (i in seq_len(n)) {\n    r \u003c- (i - 1) %/% ncol\n    c \u003c- (i - 1) %% ncol\n    ox \u003c- c * dx\n    oy \u003c- -r * dy\n    p \u003c- person_at_computer(kinds[i], ages[i], disabled[i], 1.0, ox, oy, colors[i])\n    p$icon_id \u003c- i\n    p$poly_id \u003c- paste(i, p$part, p$role)\n    polys[[i]] \u003c- p\n    if (!is.null(scores)) {\n      labels[[i]] \u003c- data.frame(x = ox + 0.2, y = oy - 0.35,\n                                 label = paste0(\"x = \", scores[i]))\n    }\n  }\n  df \u003c- do.call(rbind, polys)\n\n  plot \u003c- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, group = poly_id, fill = fill)) +\n    geom_polygon() +\n    scale_fill_identity() +\n    coord_equal() +\n    theme_void()\n\n  if (!is.null(scores)) {\n    lab_df \u003c- do.call(rbind, labels)\n    plot \u003c- plot + geom_text(data = lab_df, aes(x, y, label = label),\n                              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 5)\n  }\n\n  list(plot = plot, data = df)\n}\n\n#' A grid of icon-grids, one per \"study\" (facet_wrap(~study)) -- the icon\n#' analogue of sampling-distributions.R's plot_histogram_grid()/\n#' plot_dotpile_grid(), for showing \"many studies, each with their own\n#' independently-sampled group of people\".\n#'\n#' @param n_studies    number of study panels.\n#' @param n_per_study  number of icons (people) per study panel.\n#' @param ncol         panels per row (passed to facet_wrap).\n#' @param seed         base seed; study s uses seed + s so each panel's\n#'                     sample is independently drawn but reproducible.\n#' @param ...          passed through to testing_icons() for each panel's\n#'                     composition/colour controls (comp_kind, comp_age,\n#'                     disabled_prop, mode, skin_tones, value, dx, dy).\n#'                     `scores` isn't supported here (no labels, as for\n#'                     the single-study sample grid).\n#' @return list(plot = ggplot object, data = polygon data frame)\ntesting_icons_studies \u003c- function(n_studies, n_per_study, ncol = NULL,\n                                   seed = 1, ...) {\n  panels \u003c- vector(\"list\", n_studies)\n  for (s in seq_len(n_studies)) {\n    g \u003c- testing_icons(n = n_per_study, seed = seed + s, ...)\n    g$data$study \u003c- paste(\"Study\", s)\n    panels[[s]] \u003c- g$data\n  }\n  df \u003c- do.call(rbind, panels)\n  df$poly_id \u003c- paste(df$study, df$poly_id)\n\n  plot \u003c- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, group = poly_id, fill = fill)) +\n    geom_polygon() +\n    scale_fill_identity() +\n    coord_equal() +\n    facet_wrap(~study, ncol = ncol) +\n    theme_void() +\n    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = \"bold\"),\n          panel.spacing = unit(2, \"lines\"))\n\n  list(plot = plot, data = df)\n}\n"},"elapsedMs":0}</script></tool-result></div>

<div><tool-result call-id="toolu_01CDQVVginMKGuf8qYe3ku9M"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 20.2KB, 434 lines, showing lines 1-434]\n1\t#' ======================================...[truncated, total 22404 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 20.2KB, 434 lines, showing lines 1-434]\n#' ============================================================\n#' sampling-distributions.R\n#'\n#' Simulates scores on a hypothetical 0-40 item vocabulary test from a\n#' trial level up, and draws the figure sequence: one dot -> two dots ->\n#' a \"pile of dots\" showing a sample's distribution -> a histogram -> a\n#' grid of histograms (repeated studies) -> a scatterplot against a\n#' continuous covariate.\n#'\n#' Model (trial level up, so every observed score is *structurally*\n#' bounded to [0, n_items] -- no post-hoc clipping is needed):\n#'\n#'   Ability (logit scale):  theta_i     ~ N(theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n#'   Per-item probability:   p_i         =  plogis(theta_i)\n#'   Trial-level responses:  Y_i1..Y_i40 ~  Bernoulli(p_i)   (independent)\n#'   Observed score:         score_i     =  sum_j Y_ij        in {0,...,40}\n#'\n#' `theta_mu` and `theta_sigma` aren't set directly -- they're solved\n#' numerically (see `calibrate_ability()`) so that the *emergent* mean\n#' score matches `mu`, and the emergent parallel-forms reliability\n#' (corr(score, score') for two independent administrations drawn from\n#' the same theta_i, i.e. the same person re-tested) matches\n#' `reliability`. This mirrors real test theory: for a fixed test\n#' length, how reliable a test is and how spread out scores are, are\n#' linked to each other and to the mean, not independently free knobs --\n#' fixing `mu` and one of {`reliability`, `sd_true`} determines the\n#' other. `calibrate_ability()` (and therefore `simulate_vocab_data()` /\n#' `simulate_parallel_forms()`) accepts either: pass `reliability` (the\n#' default) when a figure is about repeatability, or pass `sd_true`\n#' directly when a figure needs independent control of spread (e.g. two\n#' panels with the same mean but visibly different spread). Whichever\n#' one wasn't the calibration target is still available afterwards as an\n#' emergent value via `calibrate_ability()$moments`.\n#'\n#' `r_with_x` is specified on the *observed*-score scale, i.e. it's\n#' (approximately) the correlation you'll actually see in\n#' `plot_scatter()`. Because measurement error attenuates any\n#' correlation involving a noisy observed variable, hitting a target\n#' observed-score correlation requires a *larger* correlation between\n#' the underlying ability and x; classical test theory gives\n#' corr(observed, true ability) = sqrt(reliability), so that attenuation\n#' is inverted internally. If `r_with_x` exceeds what's achievable at\n#' the requested `reliability` (i.e. `abs(r_with_x) > sqrt(reliability)`),\n#' it's capped and a warning is issued.\n#'\n#' Requires: ggplot2, ggdist (for the dot-pile figure).\n#'\n#' Quarto usage:\n#'   ```{r}\n#'   source(\"sampling-distributions.R\")\n#'   d \u003c- simulate_vocab_data(n = 40, seed = 1)\n#'   plot_dots(d$observed_score[1])\n#'   plot_dots(d$observed_score[1:2])\n#'   plot_dotpile(d$observed_score)\n#'   plot_histogram(d$observed_score)\n#'   plot_histogram_grid(simulate_studies(6, 40, seed = 2))\n#'   plot_scatter(simulate_vocab_data(n = 60, r_with_x = 0.5, seed = 3))\n#'   ```\n#' ============================================================\n\nlibrary(ggplot2)\n\n# ---- calibration ------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Expectation of `f(theta)` under theta ~ N(theta_mu, theta_sigma),\n#' via numerical integration (base R, no extra dependency).\nexpect_theta \u003c- function(f, theta_mu, theta_sigma) {\n  integrate(function(theta) f(theta) * dnorm(theta, theta_mu, theta_sigma),\n            lower = theta_mu - 10 * theta_sigma,\n            upper = theta_mu + 10 * theta_sigma)$value\n}\n\n#' Moments of the observed score implied by a given (theta_mu,\n#' theta_sigma, n_items), under the trial-level model described above.\n#' `var_error` uses the binomial variance n*p*(1-p) as the expected\n#' within-person sampling variance across the 40 items.\nimplied_moments \u003c- function(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items) {\n  p_bar  \u003c- expect_theta(plogis, theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n  p2_bar \u003c- expect_theta(function(th) plogis(th)^2, theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n  pq_bar \u003c- expect_theta(function(th) plogis(th) * (1 - plogis(th)), theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n\n  mean_score  \u003c- n_items * p_bar\n  var_true    \u003c- n_items^2 * (p2_bar - p_bar^2)\n  var_error   \u003c- n_items * pq_bar\n  reliability \u003c- var_true / (var_true + var_error)\n\n  list(mean_score = mean_score, var_true = var_true, var_error = var_error,\n       reliability = reliability, sd_true = sqrt(var_true),\n       sd_total = sqrt(var_true + var_error))\n}\n\n#' Solve for the (theta_mu, theta_sigma) of the ability distribution\n#' that make the trial-level model's emergent mean score match `mu`,\n#' and match *either* a target `reliability` *or* a target `sd_true`\n#' (the emergent SD of the \"true\"/expected score across people) --\n#' whichever is supplied. These two are not independently settable: for\n#' a fixed mu and n_items, specifying one determines the other, so pick\n#' whichever is more natural for the figure you're building (reliability\n#' for \"how repeatable is this test\", sd_true for \"how spread out is\n#' this population\").\n#'\n#' @param mu           target mean observed score (0 - n_items).\n#' @param reliability  target parallel-forms / test-retest reliability\n#'                      (0-1, exclusive). Used only when `sd_true` is\n#'                      NULL. Values above about 0.99 are not achievable\n#'                      for a 40-item test (they'd require an implausibly\n#'                      large ability spread) and raise an informative\n#'                      error rather than silently returning nonsense.\n#' @param sd_true      target SD, on the 0-n_items score scale, of\n#'                      people's expected/\"true\" scores (i.e. the\n#'                      between-person spread, excluding item-sampling\n#'                      noise). When supplied, this is calibrated\n#'                      directly and `reliability` is ignored. Must be\n#'                      less than the theoretical ceiling\n#'                      `sqrt(mu * (n_items - mu))` (approached only as\n#'                      the ability spread goes to infinity); requesting\n#'                      a value at or above that raises an informative\n#'                      error.\n#' @param n_items       number of trials/items (default 40).\n#' @return list(theta_mu, theta_sigma, moments) -- `moments` is the\n#'   full set of implied moments at the solution, including the\n#'   emergent `sd_true`/`sd_total`/`reliability` (whichever wasn't the\n#'   target), for inspection.\ncalibrate_ability \u003c- function(mu, reliability = 0.80, sd_true = NULL, n_items = 40) {\n  stopifnot(\"`mu` must be strictly between 0 and `n_items`\" = mu > 0 && mu \u003c n_items)\n\n  theta_mu_for_sigma \u003c- function(theta_sigma) {\n    uniroot(function(theta_mu) implied_moments(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items)$mean_score - mu,\n            lower = -15, upper = 15, extendInt = \"yes\")$root\n  }\n\n  # Robustly solve for the theta_sigma that zeroes `gap_fn`, widening the\n  # search bracket by hand rather than relying on uniroot's own\n  # extendInt = \"yes\" -- which occasionally overshoots into a theta_sigma\n  # so large that the inner theta_mu search and integrate() start\n  # returning NaN, or (near mid-scale mu) integrate() itself reports a\n  # divergent integral. A target that's only reachable out there implies\n  # an implausibly large, numerically unstable ability spread, so both\n  # failure modes are treated the same way: fail with an informative\n  # message instead of propagating a cryptic numerical error.\n  solve_theta_sigma \u003c- function(gap_fn, fail_message) {\n    gap_at \u003c- function(theta_sigma) tryCatch(gap_fn(theta_sigma), error = function(e) NA_real_)\n    lower \u003c- 0.02\n    upper \u003c- 8\n    max_upper \u003c- 128\n    g \u003c- gap_at(upper)\n    while ((is.na(g) || g \u003c 0) && upper \u003c max_upper) {\n      upper \u003c- upper * 2\n      g \u003c- gap_at(upper)\n    }\n    if (is.na(g) || g \u003c 0) stop(fail_message)\n    tryCatch(uniroot(gap_fn, lower = lower, upper = upper)$root,\n             error = function(e) stop(fail_message))\n  }\n\n  if (!is.null(sd_true)) {\n    stopifnot(\"`sd_true` must be positive\" = sd_true > 0)\n    max_sd \u003c- sqrt(mu * (n_items - mu))\n    if (sd_true >= max_sd) {\n      stop(sprintf(\n        paste(\"sd_true = %.2f is not achievable at mu = %.1f with\",\n              \"n_items = %d: the theoretical ceiling (approached only as\",\n              \"the ability spread -> infinity) is %.2f. Try a smaller sd_true.\"),\n        sd_true, mu, n_items, max_sd\n      ))\n    }\n    sd_true_gap \u003c- function(theta_sigma) {\n      theta_mu \u003c- theta_mu_for_sigma(theta_sigma)\n      implied_moments(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items)$sd_true - sd_true\n    }\n    theta_sigma \u003c- solve_theta_sigma(sd_true_gap, sprintf(\n      paste(\"sd_true = %.2f is not achievable at mu = %.1f with\",\n            \"n_items = %d (it would require a numerically unstable\",\n            \"ability spread, even though it's below the theoretical\",\n            \"ceiling of %.2f). Try a smaller sd_true.\"),\n      sd_true, mu, n_items, max_sd\n    ))\n  } else {\n    stopifnot(\n      \"`reliability` must be strictly between 0 and 1\" =\n        reliability > 0 && reliability \u003c 1\n    )\n    reliability_gap \u003c- function(theta_sigma) {\n      theta_mu \u003c- theta_mu_for_sigma(theta_sigma)\n      implied_moments(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items)$reliability - reliability\n    }\n    theta_sigma \u003c- solve_theta_sigma(reliability_gap, sprintf(\n      paste(\"reliability = %.3f is not achievable at mu = %.1f with\",\n            \"n_items = %d (it would require an implausibly large,\",\n            \"numerically unstable ability spread). Try a lower\",\n            \"reliability (\u003c= ~0.99 is usually safe) or a larger n_items.\"),\n      reliability, mu, n_items\n    ))\n  }\n\n  theta_mu \u003c- theta_mu_for_sigma(theta_sigma)\n  list(theta_mu = theta_mu, theta_sigma = theta_sigma,\n       moments = implied_moments(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items))\n}\n\n# ---- simulation -----------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Simulate one sample of vocabulary-test scores, trial level up.\n#'\n#' @param n            sample size.\n#' @param mu           target mean observed score (0-40 scale).\n#' @param reliability  target parallel-forms / test-retest reliability\n#'                      (0-1); jointly with `mu` and `n_items`, this\n#'                      determines the emergent between-person ability\n#'                      spread (see the file header). Ignored if\n#'                      `sd_true` is supplied.\n#' @param sd_true      alternate calibration target: the SD (0-n_items\n#'                      scale) of people's expected/\"true\" scores,\n#'                      calibrated directly instead of `reliability` --\n#'                      use this when a figure needs independent control\n#'                      of spread rather than of repeatability. See\n#'                      `calibrate_ability()` for the achievable range.\n#' @param r_with_x     desired correlation between the *observed* score\n#'                      and the covariate x, from -1 to 1 (0 = no\n#'                      relationship). Capped at sqrt(reliability) if\n#'                      the requested value isn't achievable, with a\n#'                      warning (`reliability` here is the emergent\n#'                      value when calibrating via `sd_true`).\n#' @param x            optional pre-specified covariate vector (length n);\n#'                      if NULL, one is drawn from N(x_mean, x_sd).\n#' @param x_mean, x_sd  mean/SD used to generate x when not supplied.\n#' @param n_items      number of trials/items (default 40, matching a\n#'                      0-40 item test).\n#' @param seed         for reproducibility.\n#'\n#' @return a data frame: id, x, theta (ability, logit scale), p_correct\n#'   (per-item probability implied by theta), observed_score (integer,\n#'   always in [0, n_items] by construction).\nsimulate_vocab_data \u003c- function(n, mu = 30, reliability = 0.80, sd_true = NULL, r_with_x = 0,\n                                 x = NULL, x_mean = 0, x_sd = 1,\n                                 n_items = 40, seed = NULL) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  if (!is.null(sd_true) && !missing(reliability)) {\n    warning(paste(\n      \"Both `reliability` and `sd_true` were supplied to\",\n      \"simulate_vocab_data(); they aren't independently settable\",\n      \"(fixing mu and sd_true determines reliability, and vice versa).\",\n      \"Using `sd_true` and ignoring `reliability`.\"\n    ))\n  }\n  cal \u003c- calibrate_ability(mu, reliability = reliability, sd_true = sd_true, n_items = n_items)\n  reliability \u003c- cal$moments$reliability\n\n  if (is.null(x)) x \u003c- rnorm(n, x_mean, x_sd)\n\n  max_r \u003c- sqrt(reliability)\n  if (abs(r_with_x) > max_r) {\n    warning(sprintf(\n      paste(\"r_with_x = %.2f is not achievable at reliability = %.2f\",\n            \"(measurement error caps the observed-score correlation at\",\n            \"about %.2f); using %.2f instead.\"),\n      r_with_x, reliability, max_r, sign(r_with_x) * max_r\n    ))\n    r_with_x \u003c- sign(r_with_x) * max_r\n  }\n  if (r_with_x != 0 && n \u003c 2) {\n    warning(\"r_with_x is not meaningful for n \u003c 2 (correlation is undefined for a single observation); ignoring it.\")\n    r_with_x \u003c- 0\n  }\n  r_theta_x \u003c- if (r_with_x == 0) 0 else r_with_x / max_r\n\n  # Only standardise x (and only use it) when it's actually needed: with\n  # r_theta_x == 0, scale(x) may be NaN (e.g. n \u003c 2, or a constant x) and\n  # 0 * NaN is NaN in R, not 0 -- multiplying it in unconditionally would\n  # silently turn every theta (and hence every score) into NA.\n  z \u003c- rnorm(n)\n  if (r_theta_x == 0) {\n    theta_z \u003c- z\n  } else {\n    xz \u003c- as.numeric(scale(x))\n    if (anyNA(xz)) {\n      warning(\"x has zero variance (e.g. all identical values); r_with_x cannot be induced. Ignoring r_with_x.\")\n      theta_z \u003c- z\n    } else {\n      theta_z \u003c- r_theta_x * xz + sqrt(1 - r_theta_x^2) * z\n    }\n  }\n  theta \u003c- cal$theta_mu + cal$theta_sigma * theta_z\n  p_correct \u003c- plogis(theta)\n\n  observed_score \u003c- rbinom(n, size = n_items, prob = p_correct)\n\n  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), x = x, theta = theta, p_correct = p_correct,\n             observed_score = observed_score)\n}\n\n#' Simulate `n_studies` independent samples of size `n_per_study`, for\n#' the \"no two samples look identical\" histogram-grid figure.\n#' Returns one long data frame with a `study` id column.\nsimulate_studies \u003c- function(n_studies, n_per_study, seed = NULL, ...) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  out \u003c- lapply(seq_len(n_studies), function(s) {\n    d \u003c- simulate_vocab_data(n_per_study, seed = NULL, ...)\n    d$study \u003c- paste(\"Study\", s)\n    d\n  })\n  do.call(rbind, out)\n}\n\n#' Two independent administrations (parallel forms / test-retest) per\n#' person, sharing the same ability theta_i, to check/demonstrate the\n#' calibrated reliability directly (corr(form1, form2) ~ reliability).\n#' @param sd_true  alternate calibration target in place of `reliability`\n#'                  -- see `simulate_vocab_data()` / `calibrate_ability()`.\nsimulate_parallel_forms \u003c- function(n, mu = 30, reliability = 0.80, sd_true = NULL,\n                                     n_items = 40, seed = NULL) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  if (!is.null(sd_true) && !missing(reliability)) {\n    warning(paste(\n      \"Both `reliability` and `sd_true` were supplied to\",\n      \"simulate_parallel_forms(); they aren't independently settable.\",\n      \"Using `sd_true` and ignoring `reliability`.\"\n    ))\n  }\n  cal \u003c- calibrate_ability(mu, reliability = reliability, sd_true = sd_true, n_items = n_items)\n  theta \u003c- rnorm(n, cal$theta_mu, cal$theta_sigma)\n  p_correct \u003c- plogis(theta)\n  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), theta = theta, p_correct = p_correct,\n             form1 = rbinom(n, n_items, p_correct),\n             form2 = rbinom(n, n_items, p_correct))\n}\n\n# ---- figures ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' One or two scores plotted as points on a number line.\nplot_dots \u003c- function(scores, xlim = c(0, 40)) {\n  # y nudged just above 0 so the dot rests on top of the axis line\n  # rather than being bisected by it.\n  df \u003c- data.frame(score = scores, y = 0.04)\n  ggplot(df, aes(score, y)) +\n    geom_point(size = 6, color = \"#3B6EA5\") +\n    scale_x_continuous(name = \"Score (items correct)\") +\n    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.5), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +\n    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +\n    theme_minimal() +\n    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),\n          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),\n          axis.line.x = element_line(color = \"black\", linewidth = 0.9),\n          axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = \"black\"))\n}\n\n#' A sample's scores as a \"pile of dots\" (ggdist::stat_dots) -- shows\n#' the distribution as discrete points, not a smoothed density/histogram.\nplot_dotpile \u003c- function(scores, xlim = c(0, 40), ...) {\n  if (!requireNamespace(\"ggdist\", quietly = TRUE)) {\n    stop(\"Package 'ggdist' is required for plot_dotpile(). Install with install.packages('ggdist').\")\n  }\n  df \u003c- data.frame(score = scores)\n  ggplot(df, aes(x = score)) +\n    ggdist::stat_dots(color = \"#3B6EA5\", fill = \"#3B6EA5\", ...) +\n    scale_x_continuous(name = \"Score (items correct)\") +\n    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +\n    theme_minimal() +\n    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),\n          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),\n          axis.line.x = element_line(color = \"black\", linewidth = 0.9),\n          axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = \"black\"))\n}\n\n#' A grid of \"pile of dots\" distributions, one per \"study\" -- the\n#' ggdist::stat_dots analogue of plot_histogram_grid(), for showing\n#' sampling variability as discrete points rather than binned counts.\n#' @param data a data frame with a `study` and `observed_score` column,\n#'   e.g. from simulate_studies().\n#' @param binwidth dot diameter in data units (score points). ggdist's\n#'   default computes a separate binwidth per facet panel, sized to\n#'   stack that panel's tallest pile within the available height --\n#'   which makes dots different sizes across panels. Fixing binwidth\n#'   here keeps every panel's dots the same size.\nplot_dotpile_grid \u003c- function(data, value_col = \"observed_score\",\n                               xlim = c(0, 40), ncol = NULL, binwidth = 2.5, ...) {\n  if (!requireNamespace(\"ggdist\", quietly = TRUE)) {\n    stop(\"Package 'ggdist' is required for plot_dotpile_grid(). Install with install.packages('ggdist').\")\n  }\n  data$.value \u003c- data[[value_col]]\n  ggplot(data, aes(x = .value)) +\n    ggdist::stat_dots(color = \"#3B6EA5\", fill = \"#3B6EA5\", binwidth = binwidth, ...) +\n    scale_x_continuous(name = \"Score (items correct)\") +\n    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +\n    facet_wrap(~study, ncol = ncol) +\n    theme_minimal() +\n    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),\n          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),\n          strip.text = element_text(face = \"bold\"),\n          panel.spacing = unit(2, \"lines\"),\n          axis.line.x = element_line(color = \"black\", linewidth = 0.9),\n          axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = \"black\"))\n}\n\n#' A histogram of one sample's scores.\nplot_histogram \u003c- function(scores, binwidth = 1, xlim = c(0, 40)) {\n  df \u003c- data.frame(score = scores)\n  ggplot(df, aes(x = score)) +\n    geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth, fill = \"#3B6EA5\", color = \"white\") +\n    scale_x_continuous(name = \"Score (items correct)\") +\n    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +\n    ylab(\"Count\") +\n    theme_minimal()\n}\n\n#' A grid of histograms, one per \"study\", to show sampling variability\n#' across repeated samples from the same population.\n#' @param data a data frame with a `study` and `observed_score` column,\n#'   e.g. from simulate_studies().\nplot_histogram_grid \u003c- function(data, value_col = \"observed_score\",\n                                 binwidth = 1, xlim = c(0, 40), ncol = NULL) {\n  data$.value \u003c- data[[value_col]]\n  ggplot(data, aes(x = .value)) +\n    geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth, fill = \"#3B6EA5\", color = \"white\") +\n    scale_x_continuous(name = \"Score (items correct)\") +\n    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +\n    ylab(\"Count\") +\n    facet_wrap(~study, ncol = ncol) +\n    theme_minimal() +\n    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = \"bold\"))\n}\n\n#' Scatterplot of score against the continuous covariate, with a fitted\n#' line, to illustrate the (settable) correlation.\nplot_scatter \u003c- function(data, x_col = \"x\", y_col = \"observed_score\", show_fit = TRUE) {\n  df \u003c- data.frame(x = data[[x_col]], y = data[[y_col]])\n  p \u003c- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +\n    geom_point(color = \"#3B6EA5\", alpha = 0.8) +\n    xlab(x_col) + ylab(\"Score (items correct)\") +\n    theme_minimal()\n  if (show_fit) p \u003c- p + geom_smooth(method = \"lm\", se = TRUE, color = \"#B23A48\")\n  p\n}\n"},"elapsedMs":6}</script></tool-result></div>

Fewer, bigger shapes read better than several small ones once\n    # icons are shrunk down in a grid.\n    parts[[\"torso\"]] \u003c- data.frame(\n      x = c(-0.30, 0.30, 0.30, -0.30),\n      y = c(1.28, 1.28, 0.62, 0.62)\n    )\n    parts[[\"wheel\"]] \u003c- circle_pts(0.00, 0.28, 0.34, n = 32)\n    parts[[\"footrest\"]] \u003c- data.frame(\n      x = c(0.34, 0.50, 0.50, 0.34),\n      y = c(0.02, 0.02, 0.12, 0.12)\n    )\n  } else {\n    parts[[\"torso\"]] \u003c- data.frame(\n      x = c(-0.34, 0.34, 0.20, -0.20),\n      y = c(1.30, 1.30, 0.72, 0.72)\n    )\n\n    if (kind == \"A\") {           # trouser legs: two bars with a slim gap\n      parts[[\"leg_l\"]] \u003c- data.frame(x = c(-0.20, -0.03, -0.06, -0.20),\n                                      y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\n      parts[[\"leg_r\"]] \u003c- data.frame(x = c(0.03, 0.20, 0.20, 0.06),\n                                      y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\n    } else if (kind == \"B\") {    # skirt\n      parts[[\"legs\"]] \u003c- data.frame(x = c(-0.20, 0.20, 0.46, -0.46),\n                                     y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\n    } else if (kind == \"N\") {    # half trouser (left) / half skirt (right)\n      parts[[\"leg_l\"]] \u003c- data.frame(x = c(-0.20, -0.02, -0.05, -0.20),\n                                      y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\n      parts[[\"legs_skirt_half\"]] \u003c- data.frame(x = c(0.00, 0.20, 0.46, 0.00),\n                                                y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\n    }\n\n    if (age == \"elder\") {\n      parts[[\"cane\"]] \u003c- data.frame(x = c(0.36, 0.40, 0.58, 0.54),\n                                     y = c(0.78, 0.78, 0.02, 0.02))\n    }\n  }\n\n  # apply scale (child = smaller) then offset into the grid position\n  out \u003c- lapply(names(parts), function(nm) {\n    p \u003c- parts[[nm]]\n    data.frame(part = nm, x = ox + scale * p$x, y = oy + scale * p$y)\n  })\n  do.call(rbind, out)\n}\n\n# ---- composition sampling -----------------------------------------------\n\n#' Largest-remainder sampling: turns a named vector of proportions into\n#' exactly `n` labels, hitting the target proportions as closely as\n#' integer counts allow, then shuffles their order.\nsample_counts \u003c- function(n, props, seed) {\n  stopifnot(\n    \"`props` must have non-negative values, with at least one positive\" =\n      all(props >= 0) && sum(props) > 0\n  )\n  props \u003c- props / sum(props)\n  set.seed(seed)\n  raw \u003c- props * n\n  counts \u003c- floor(raw)\n  remainder \u003c- n - sum(counts)\n  if (remainder > 0) {\n    order \u003c- order(-(raw - counts))\n    for (i in seq_len(remainder)) {\n      idx \u003c- order[((i - 1) %% length(order)) + 1]\n      counts[idx] \u003c- counts[idx] + 1\n    }\n  }\n  sample(rep(names(props), counts))\n}\n\n# ---- colour -----------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Map a numeric value to a symmetric diverging colour, vivid at both\n#' extremes and light at zero (the \"null effect\" point). `value` need\n#' not be centred on the data -- 0 is always treated as the reference\n#' point, so effect sizes / differences map intuitively.\n#'\n#' Default endpoints are blue/orange from the Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe\n#' palette (distinguishable under deuteranopia, protanopia, and\n#' tritanopia) rather than a red/blue or red/green diverging scale.\ndiverging_colors \u003c- function(value, neg = \"#0072B2\", mid = \"#F2F1EC\", pos = \"#E69F00\") {\n  span \u003c- max(abs(value), 1e-9)\n  tt \u003c- value / span                     # -1 .. 1, 0 = null\n  ramp_lo \u003c- grDevices::colorRamp(c(neg, mid))\n  ramp_hi \u003c- grDevices::colorRamp(c(mid, pos))\n  to_hex \u003c- function(m) grDevices::rgb(m[, 1], m[, 2], m[, 3], maxColorValue = 255)\n  vapply(tt, function(t) {\n    if (t \u003c= 0) to_hex(ramp_lo(t + 1))\n    else        to_hex(ramp_hi(t))\n  }, character(1))\n}\n\n# ---- automatic grid shape -----------------------------------------------\n\n#' Pick the `ncol` (icons per row) that makes an n-icon grid's bounding\n#' box (`ncol * dx` wide by `ceiling(n / ncol) * dy` tall) match a target\n#' width:height `aspect` ratio as closely as possible -- e.g. so the\n#' figure fills a 16:9 slide with minimal leftover margin either way.\nchoose_ncol \u003c- function(n, dx, dy, aspect) {\n  ncols \u003c- seq_len(n)\n  nrows \u003c- ceiling(n / ncols)\n  grid_ratio \u003c- (ncols * dx) / (nrows * dy)\n  # log-ratio distance treats \"twice too wide\" and \"twice too tall\"\n  # as equally bad, so it doesn't systematically favour wide grids.\n  ncols[which.min(abs(log(grid_ratio / aspect)))]\n}\n\n# ---- main function ------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Build a grid of person pictograms.\n#'\n#' @param n           number of icons.\n#' @param ncol        icons per row (rows are computed from n). Leave as\n#'                    `\"auto\"` (the default) to pick the layout that best\n#'                    fills a window of the given `aspect` ratio, or pass\n#'                    an integer to fix it yourself.\n#' @param aspect      target width:height ratio used only when\n#'                    `ncol = \"auto\"`. Defaults to 16/9. Set this to match\n#'                    your actual slide size (e.g. `revealjs`'s default\n#'                    is 960/700; a custom `width`/`height` in the format\n#'                    YAML should be reflected here) so the grid fills\n#'                    the slide with as little leftover margin as\n#'                    possible.\n#' @param comp_kind   named proportions for silhouette: \"A\" (trouser-\n#'                    coded), \"B\" (skirt-coded), \"N\" (half/half --\n#'                    reads as a non-binary / trans-inclusive icon).\n#' @param comp_age    named proportions for \"adult\", \"child\", \"elder\".\n#' @param disabled_prop proportion of icons shown using the wheelchair\n#'                    silhouette.\n#' @param mode        \"diversity\" (discrete skin-tone fill, sampled) or\n#'                    \"value\" (continuous diverging fill driven by\n#'                    `value`).\n#' @param skin_tones  hex colours to sample from when mode = \"diversity\".\n#' @param value       numeric vector of length n; required when\n#'                    mode = \"value\". 0 = the null/reference point.\n#' @param seed        for reproducibility.\n#'\n#' @return a list with `plot` (a ggplot object), `data` (the full\n#'   polygon data frame, if you want to customise further), `meta`\n#'   (per-icon kind/age/disabled/fill), and `alt_text` (a plain-language\n#'   summary of the composition, generated from the same sampling used\n#'   to draw the icons -- pass it straight into `fig-alt`).\nperson_grid \u003c- function(n = 30, ncol = \"auto\", aspect = 16 / 9,\n                         comp_kind = c(A = 0.45, B = 0.45, N = 0.10),\n                         comp_age = c(adult = 0.70, child = 0.15, elder = 0.15),\n                         disabled_prop = 0.12,\n                         mode = c(\"diversity\", \"value\"),\n                         skin_tones = c(\"#4A3728\", \"#7A5230\", \"#B07A4E\",\n                                        \"#D9A066\", \"#F0C892\", \"#F5E1C8\"),\n                         value = NULL,\n                         seed = 1,\n                         dx = 1.15, dy = 2.15) {\n  mode \u003c- match.arg(mode)\n  if (identical(ncol, \"auto\")) ncol \u003c- choose_ncol(n, dx, dy, aspect)\n  nrow_ \u003c- ceiling(n / ncol)\n\n  kinds \u003c- sample_counts(n, comp_kind, seed)\n  ages \u003c- sample_counts(n, comp_age, seed + 1)\n  disabled \u003c- sample_counts(n, c(yes = disabled_prop, no = 1 - disabled_prop), seed + 2) == \"yes\"\n\n  if (mode == \"diversity\") {\n    set.seed(seed + 3)\n    fill \u003c- sample(skin_tones, n, replace = TRUE)\n  } else {\n    stopifnot(\"`value` must be supplied and length n when mode = 'value'\" =\n                !is.null(value) && length(value) == n)\n    fill \u003c- diverging_colors(value)\n  }\n\n  polys \u003c- vector(\"list\", n)\n  for (i in seq_len(n)) {\n    r \u003c- (i - 1) %/% ncol\n    c \u003c- (i - 1) %% ncol\n    ox \u003c- c * dx\n    oy \u003c- -r * dy\n    scale \u003c- if (ages[i] == \"child\") 0.65 else 1.0\n    p \u003c- person_parts(kinds[i], ages[i], disabled[i], scale, ox, oy)\n    p$icon_id \u003c- i\n    p$poly_id \u003c- paste(i, p$part)\n    p$fill \u003c- fill[i]\n    polys[[i]] \u003c- p\n  }\n  df \u003c- do.call(rbind, polys)\n\n  # No expansion/margins: the panel should be exactly the icons' bounding\n  # box, so that when Reveal stretches the image to fill the slide there\n  # is no leftover white border eating into the \"fill the window\" effect.\n  plot \u003c- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, group = poly_id, fill = fill)) +\n    geom_polygon() +\n    scale_fill_identity() +\n    coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +\n    theme_void() +\n    theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))\n\n  meta \u003c- data.frame(icon_id = seq_len(n), kind = kinds, age = ages,\n                      disabled = disabled, fill = fill)\n\n  alt_text \u003c- if (mode == \"diversity\") {\n    sprintf(\n      \"Grid of %d person icons of varying skin tone, gender presentation, and age, illustrating sample diversity. %d%% shown as children, %d%% as older adults, and %d%% using a wheelchair icon.\",\n      n,\n      round(100 * mean(ages == \"child\")),\n      round(100 * mean(ages == \"elder\")),\n      round(100 * mean(disabled))\n    )\n  } else {\n    sprintf(\n      \"Grid of %d person icons coloured on a diverging scale from %.2f to %.2f, blue for negative values, near-white at zero, orange for positive values.\",\n      n, min(value), max(value)\n    )\n  }\n\n  list(plot = plot, data = df, meta = meta, alt_text = alt_text)\n}\n"},"elapsedMs":5}</script></tool-result></div>

Confirmed the full document renders cleanly via `quarto render`.\n\n## User\n\nI developed two scripts: testing-sequence.R, and sampling-distributions.R. I need to be able to generate both sets of images parametrically so that (1.) the figure images should be capable of the same color or shape variation permitted previously, and I should be able to generate grids of as many figure images as required (2.) the synthetic data simulation based images should be capable of variation with respect to the mean and the SD of distributions. The basis for the synthetic data simulation is: (1.) measurement error framework y = a + bx_i + e_i where e_i can reflect measurement error, and errors e_1 ... e_n can be considered a random sample from a distribution mean mean 0 and standard deviation \\sigma. Let's assume that the task for data collection is like the Shipley vocabulary test: participants respond to total 40 multiple choice questions; they can get 0-40 responses correct. Most of the time, adult university students might get responses distributed around 20-40 with a skew towards higher scores. Let's simplify things and assume that the distribution is normal. Let's not tie the simulations specifically to the Shipley but say that is it a vocabulary test of some kind where the observation or trial level response is the accuracy of response made by a participant to a test item. Let's say that there is some measurement error (the test is good but not perfect) so that if a participant did two equivalent alternate versions of the test, their scores would correlate quite highly (~ 80%) or if they did the same test twice, their scores would correlate quite highly (~80%) ignoring the effect of test-retest repetition priming. Let's say that if we did a series of studies, testing in each study a sample of participants, the distribution of scores would resemble the normal (more closely, for larger samples) but there is sampling error so that no distribution of scores would be exactly the same as the other. Let's say that the data generating process is capable of resulting in the simulation of a dataset in which outcome accuracy is correlated to a continuous numeric variable (e.g., age, or reading experience). The simulations should be set up so that the degree of correlation can be varied as a parameter from 0 to either negative or positive correlations. I think I need two sets of scripts, one to do the icon images (one person, two people, grid of people), a second to do data simulations and figure generation: dot, pile of dots, histogram, scatterplot. I want you to critically evaluate the scripts. ============================================================\\n#' testing-sequence.R\\n#'\\n#' Extends person-grid.R with a \\\"person at a computer\\\" composite icon,\\n#' for the narrative sequence: one person doing the task -> two people\\n#' doing the task -> a whole sample doing the task (grid, no scores\\n#' shown). Same silhouette/age/disability/colour parametrization as\\n#' person-grid.R carries straight over.\\n#'\\n#' Requires person-grid.R to be sourced first (same folder).\\n#'\\n#' Quarto usage:\\n#'   ```{r}\\n#'   source(\\\"person-grid.R\\\")\\n#'   source(\\\"testing-sequence.R\\\")\\n#'   testing_icons(n = 1, scores = 27)$plot\\n#'   testing_icons(n = 2, scores = c(31, 24))$plot\\n#'   testing_icons(n = 30, seed = 7)$plot   # no `scores` -> sample, no labels\\n#'   ```\\n#' ============================================================\\n\\nlibrary(ggplot2)\\n\\n# ---- monitor/computer geometry -------------------------------------------\\n\\nmonitor_parts \\u003c- function(scale = 1, ox = 0, oy = 0) {\\n  parts \\u003c- list(\\n    bezel  = data.frame(x = c(-0.34, 0.34, 0.34, -0.34), y = c(0.62, 0.62, 0.20, 0.20)),\\n    screen = data.frame(x = c(-0.28, 0.28, 0.28, -0.28), y = c(0.56, 0.56, 0.26, 0.26)),\\n    neck   = data.frame(x = c(-0.04, 0.04, 0.04, -0.04), y = c(0.20, 0.20, 0.10, 0.10)),\\n    base   = data.frame(x = c(-0.20, 0.20, 0.20, -0.20), y = c(0.10, 0.10, 0.04, 0.04))\\n  )\\n  out \\u003c- lapply(names(parts), function(nm) {\\n    p \\u003c- parts[[nm]]\\n    data.frame(part = nm, x = ox + scale * p$x, y = oy + scale * p$y)\\n  })\\n  do.call(rbind, out)\\n}\\n\\n#' One person + monitor, as a single composite polygon set with a `role`\\n#' column (\\\"person\\\" vs \\\"monitor\\\") so they can be filled differently.\\nperson_at_computer \\u003c- function(kind = \\\"A\\\", age = \\\"adult\\\", disabled = FALSE,\\n                                scale = 1, ox = 0, oy = 0,\\n                                person_color = \\\"#3B6EA5\\\",\\n                                screen_color = \\\"#CFE8FF\\\",\\n                                frame_color = \\\"#555555\\\") {\\n  p \\u003c- person_parts(kind, age, disabled, scale, ox, oy)\\n  p$role \\u003c- \\\"person\\\"\\n  p$fill \\u003c- person_color\\n\\n  m \\u003c- monitor_parts(scale = scale * 0.9, ox = ox + scale * 0.75, oy = oy + scale * 0.05)\\n  m$role \\u003c- \\\"monitor\\\"\\n  m$fill \\u003c- ifelse(m$part == \\\"screen\\\", screen_color, frame_color)\\n\\n  rbind(p, m)\\n}\\n\\n# ---- main sequence function -----------------------------------------------\\n\\n#' Draw n copies of \\\"person at computer\\\".\\n#'\\n#' @param n        how many icons (1 = single participant, 2 = a pair,\\n#'                 larger = a sample).\\n#' @param scores   optional numeric vector of length n; if supplied, each\\n#'                 icon gets an \\\"x = \\u003cscore>\\\" label underneath (used for\\n#'                 the n = 1 and n = 2 steps). Leave NULL for the sample\\n#'                 grid step, where individual scores aren't shown.\\n#' @param ncol     icons per row; default is n itself for n \\u003c= 4, else\\n#'                 a compact grid.\\n#' @param comp_kind, comp_age, disabled_prop, skin_tones, seed: same\\n#'                 composition/colour controls as person_grid().\\n#' @return list(plot = ggplot object, data = polygon data frame)\\ntesting_icons \\u003c- function(n, scores = NULL, ncol = NULL,\\n                           comp_kind = c(A = 0.45, B = 0.45, N = 0.10),\\n                           comp_age = c(adult = 1.0),\\n                           disabled_prop = 0,\\n                           skin_tones = c(\\\"#4A3728\\\", \\\"#7A5230\\\", \\\"#B07A4E\\\",\\n                                          \\\"#D9A066\\\", \\\"#F0C892\\\", \\\"#F5E1C8\\\"),\\n                           seed = 1, dx = 1.9, dy = 2.5) {\\n  if (!is.null(scores)) stopifnot(length(scores) == n)\\n  if (is.null(ncol)) ncol \\u003c- if (n \\u003c= 4) n else min(6, ceiling(sqrt(n)))\\n  nrow_ \\u003c- ceiling(n / ncol)\\n\\n  kinds \\u003c- sample_counts(n, comp_kind, seed)\\n  ages \\u003c- sample_counts(n, comp_age, seed + 1)\\n  disabled \\u003c- sample_counts(n, c(yes = disabled_prop, no = 1 - disabled_prop), seed + 2) == \\\"yes\\\"\\n  set.seed(seed + 3)\\n  colors \\u003c- sample(skin_tones, n, replace = TRUE)\\n\\n  polys \\u003c- vector(\\\"list\\\", n)\\n  labels \\u003c- vector(\\\"list\\\", n)\\n  for (i in seq_len(n)) {\\n    r \\u003c- (i - 1) %/% ncol\\n    c \\u003c- (i - 1) %% ncol\\n    ox \\u003c- c * dx\\n    oy \\u003c- -r * dy\\n    p \\u003c- person_at_computer(kinds[i], ages[i], disabled[i], 1.0, ox, oy, colors[i])\\n    p$icon_id \\u003c- i\\n    p$poly_id \\u003c- paste(i, p$part, p$role)\\n    polys[[i]] \\u003c- p\\n    if (!is.null(scores)) {\\n      labels[[i]] \\u003c- data.frame(x = ox + 0.2, y = oy - 0.35,\\n                                 label = paste0(\\\"x = \\\", scores[i]))\\n    }\\n  }\\n  df \\u003c- do.call(rbind, polys)\\n\\n  plot \\u003c- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, group = poly_id, fill = fill)) +\\n    geom_polygon() +\\n    scale_fill_identity() +\\n    coord_equal() +\\n    theme_void()\\n\\n  if (!is.null(scores)) {\\n    lab_df \\u003c- do.call(rbind, labels)\\n    plot \\u003c- plot + geom_text(data = lab_df, aes(x, y, label = label),\\n                              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 5)\\n  }\\n\\n  list(plot = plot, data = df)\\n}\\n\"},\"elapsedMs\":1}\u003c/script>\u003c/tool-result>\u003c/div>\n\n\u003cdiv>\u003ctool-result 1-169]\\n1\\t#' =======================================...[truncated, total 8042 chars]\"},\"resultPreview\":{\"type\":\"code\",\"value\":\"[File: 7.3KB, 169 lines, showing lines 1-169]\\n#' ============================================================\\n#' sampling-distributions.R\\n#'\\n#' Simulates scores on a hypothetical 0-40 item vocabulary test under a\\n#' simple classical-test-theory measurement model, and draws the\\n#' figure sequence: one dot -> two dots -> a \\\"pile of dots\\\" showing a\\n#' sample's distribution -> a histogram -> a grid of histograms\\n#' (repeated studies) -> a scatterplot against a continuous covariate.\\n#'\\n#' Model:\\n#'   True score:      T_i  = mu + sd_true * (r*z_x + sqrt(1-r^2)*z_i)\\n#'   Observed score:  Y_i  = T_i + e_i,  e_i ~ N(0, sigma_meas)\\n#'\\n#' where z_x is the covariate (e.g. age, reading experience) in\\n#' standardised form, r is the desired population correlation between\\n#' true score and the covariate (settable from -1 to 1), and\\n#' sigma_meas is chosen so that the test-retest / parallel-forms\\n#' reliability (corr between two independent measurements of the same\\n#' true score) equals `reliability` (default 0.80, per the ~80%\\n#' correlation you'd expect from two equivalent forms of a decent\\n#' vocabulary test).\\n#'\\n#' Requires: ggplot2, ggdist (for the dot-pile figure).\\n#'\\n#' Quarto usage:\\n#'   ```{r}\\n#'   source(\\\"sampling-distributions.R\\\")\\n#'   d \\u003c- simulate_vocab_data(n = 40, seed = 1)\\n#'   plot_dots(d$observed_score[1])\\n#'   plot_dots(d$observed_score[1:2])\\n#'   plot_dotpile(d$observed_score)\\n#'   plot_histogram(d$observed_score)\\n#'   plot_histogram_grid(simulate_studies(6, 40, seed = 2))\\n#'   plot_scatter(simulate_vocab_data(n = 60, r_with_x = 0.5, seed = 3))\\n#'   ```\\n#' ============================================================\\n\\nlibrary(ggplot2)\\n\\n# ---- simulation -----------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n#' Simulate one sample of vocabulary-test scores.\\n#'\\n#' @param n            sample size.\\n#' @param mu           mean true score (0-40 scale).\\n#' @param sd_true      SD of true score across people.\\n#' @param reliability  parallel-forms / test-retest reliability (0-1);\\n#'                     controls how much measurement error is added.\\n#' @param r_with_x     desired correlation between true score and the\\n#'                      covariate x, from -1 to 1. 0 = no relationship.\\n#' @param x            optional pre-specified covariate vector (length n);\\n#'                      if NULL, one is drawn from N(x_mean, x_sd).\\n#' @param x_mean, x_sd  mean/SD used to generate x when not supplied.\\n#' @param max_score    ceiling for the test (0-40 by default); scores\\n#'                      are clipped and rounded to whole items correct.\\n#' @param seed         for reproducibility.\\n#'\\n#' @return a data frame: id, x, true_score, observed_score (continuous),\\n#'   accuracy (rounded/clipped to [0, max_score]).\\nsimulate_vocab_data \\u003c- function(n, mu = 30, sd_true = 5, reliability = 0.80,\\n                                 r_with_x = 0, x = NULL, x_mean = 0, x_sd = 1,\\n                                 max_score = 40, seed = NULL) {\\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\\n  if (is.null(x)) x \\u003c- rnorm(n, x_mean, x_sd)\\n  xz \\u003c- as.numeric(scale(x))\\n  z \\u003c- rnorm(n)\\n  Tz \\u003c- r_with_x * xz + sqrt(1 - r_with_x^2) * z   # corr(Tz, xz) = r_with_x\\n  true_score \\u003c- mu + sd_true * Tz\\n\\n  sigma_meas \\u003c- sd_true * sqrt((1 - reliability) / reliability)\\n  e \\u003c- rnorm(n, 0, sigma_meas)\\n  observed_score \\u003c- true_score + e\\n  accuracy \\u003c- round(pmin(pmax(observed_score, 0), max_score))\\n\\n  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), x = x, true_score = true_score,\\n             observed_score = observed_score, accuracy = accuracy)\\n}\\n\\n#' Simulate `n_studies` independent samples of size `n_per_study`, for\\n#' the \\\"no two samples look identical\\\" histogram-grid figure.\\n#' Returns one long data frame with a `study` id column.\\nsimulate_studies \\u003c- function(n_studies, n_per_study, seed = NULL, ...) {\\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\\n  out \\u003c- lapply(seq_len(n_studies), function(s) {\\n    d \\u003c- simulate_vocab_data(n_per_study, seed = NULL, ...)\\n    d$study \\u003c- paste(\\\"Study\\\", s)\\n    d\\n  })\\n  do.call(rbind, out)\\n}\\n\\n#' Two parallel-forms scores per person, to check/demonstrate the\\n#' ~0.80 reliability directly (corr(Y1, Y2) ~ reliability).\\nsimulate_parallel_forms \\u003c- function(n, mu = 30, sd_true = 5, reliability = 0.80, seed = NULL) {\\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\\n  true_score \\u003c- rnorm(n, mu, sd_true)\\n  sigma_meas \\u003c- sd_true * sqrt((1 - reliability) / reliability)\\n  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), true_score = true_score,\\n             form1 = true_score + rnorm(n, 0, sigma_meas),\\n             form2 = true_score + rnorm(n, 0, sigma_meas))\\n}\\n\\n# ---- figures ----------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n#' One or two scores plotted as points on a number line.\\nplot_dots \\u003c- function(scores, xlim = c(0, 40)) {\\n  df \\u003c- data.frame(score = scores, y = 0)\\n  ggplot(df, aes(score, y)) +\\n    geom_point(size = 6, color = \\\"#3B6EA5\\\") +\\n    scale_x_continuous(limits = xlim, name = \\\"Score (items correct)\\\") +\\n    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.5, 0.5)) +\\n    theme_minimal() +\\n    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),\\n          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())\\n}\\n\\n#' A sample's scores as a \\\"pile of dots\\\" (ggdist::stat_dots) -- shows\\n#' the distribution as discrete points, not a smoothed density/histogram.\\nplot_dotpile \\u003c- function(scores, xlim = c(0, 40), ...) {\\n  if (!requireNamespace(\\\"ggdist\\\", quietly = TRUE)) {\\n    stop(\\\"Package 'ggdist' is required for plot_dotpile(). Install with install.packages('ggdist').\\\")\\n  }\\n  df \\u003c- data.frame(score = scores)\\n  ggplot(df, aes(x = score)) +\\n    ggdist::stat_dots(color = \\\"#3B6EA5\\\", fill = \\\"#3B6EA5\\\", ...) +\\n    scale_x_continuous(limits = xlim, name = \\\"Score (items correct)\\\") +\\n    theme_minimal() +\\n    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),\\n          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())\\n}\\n\\n#' A histogram of one sample's scores.\\nplot_histogram \\u003c- function(scores, binwidth = 1, xlim = c(0, 40)) {\\n  df \\u003c- data.frame(score = scores)\\n  ggplot(df, aes(x = score)) +\\n    geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth, fill = \\\"#3B6EA5\\\", color = \\\"white\\\") +\\n    scale_x_continuous(limits = xlim, name = \\\"Score (items correct)\\\") +\\n    ylab(\\\"Count\\\") +\\n    theme_minimal()\\n}\\n\\n#' A grid of histograms, one per \\\"study\\\", to show sampling variability\\n#' across repeated samples from the same population.\\n#' @param data a data frame with a `study` and `accuracy`/`observed_score`\\n#'   column, e.g. from simulate_studies().\\nplot_histogram_grid \\u003c- function(data, value_col = \\\"observed_score\\\",\\n                                 binwidth = 1, xlim = c(0, 40), ncol = NULL) {\\n  data$.value \\u003c- data[[value_col]]\\n  ggplot(data, aes(x = .value)) +\\n    geom_histogram(binwidth = binwidth, fill = \\\"#3B6EA5\\\", color = \\\"white\\\") +\\n    scale_x_continuous(limits = xlim, name = \\\"Score (items correct)\\\") +\\n    ylab(\\\"Count\\\") +\\n    facet_wrap(~study, ncol = ncol) +\\n    theme_minimal() +\\n    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = \\\"bold\\\"))\\n}\\n\\n#' Scatterplot of score against the continuous covariate, with a fitted\\n#' line, to illustrate the (settable) correlation.\\nplot_scatter \\u003c- function(data, x_col = \\\"x\\\", y_col = \\\"observed_score\\\", show_fit = TRUE) {\\n  df \\u003c- data.frame(x = data[[x_col]], y = data[[y_col]])\\n  p \\u003c- ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +\\n    geom_point(color = \\\"#3B6EA5\\\", alpha = 0.8) +\\n    xlab(x_col) + ylab(\\\"Score (items correct)\\\") +\\n    theme_minimal()\\n  if (show_fit) p \\u003c- p + geom_smooth(method = \\\"lm\\\", se = TRUE, color = \\\"#B23A48\\\")\\n  p\\n}\\n\"},\"elapsedMs\":1}\u003c/script>\u003c/tool-result>\u003c/div>\n\n\u003cdiv>\u003ctool-result call-id=\"toolu_01De2VGhwZYtiXXMZuhzfgmz\">\u003cscript ============================================================\\n#' person-grid.R\\n#'\\n#' A parametrized \\\"restroom-sign style\\\" pictogram generator, built with\\n#' plain polygons in ggplot2 (no external icon fonts, so it renders\\n#' identically everywhere Quarto builds the book).\\n#'\\n#' Each icon is assembled from a few flat shapes:\\n#'   - head          (circle)\\n#'   - torso         (trapezoid)\\n#'   - legs          (\\\"A\\\" = trouser silhouette, \\\"B\\\" = skirt silhouette,\\n#'                     \\\"N\\\" = half trouser / half skirt -- an inclusive,\\n#'                     non-binary-coded silhouette)\\n#'   - wheelchair    (swapped in for the legs when disabled = TRUE)\\n#'   - cane          (added when age = \\\"elder\\\")\\n#'   - overall scale (reduced when age = \\\"child\\\")\\n#'\\n#' Colour is decided by ONE of two modes, chosen by whether you pass\\n#' `value=`:\\n#'   mode = \\\"diversity\\\" (default): each icon's fill is sampled from a\\n#'          discrete set of skin tones -- for showing sample diversity.\\n#'   mode = \\\"value\\\": each icon's fill is placed on a continuous,\\n#'          symmetric diverging scale (dark negative -> light null ->\\n#'          dark positive) driven by a numeric `value` per icon -- for\\n#'          showing an effect size, a score, a probability, etc.\\n#'\\n#' Use in a Quarto R chunk:\\n#'\\n#'   ```{r}\\n#'   #| label: fig-diversity-sample\\n#'   #| fig-cap: \\\"A hypothetical study sample\\\"\\n#'   #| fig-alt: !expr diversity_grid$alt_text\\n#'   source(\\\"person-grid.R\\\")\\n#'   diversity_grid \\u003c- person_grid(n = 30, seed = 7)\\n#'   diversity_grid$plot\\n#'   ```\\n#' ============================================================\\n\\nlibrary(ggplot2)\\n\\n# ---- low-level geometry -------------------------------------------------\\n\\ncircle_pts \\u003c- function(cx, cy, r, n = 24) {\\n  t \\u003c- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n + 1)[-(n + 1)]\\n  data.frame(x = cx + r * cos(t), y = cy + r * sin(t))\\n}\\n\\n#' Build the list of sub-polygons for one icon, in local coordinates,\\n#' then offset by (ox, oy) and multiplied by `scale`.\\nperson_parts \\u003c- function(kind = c(\\\"A\\\", \\\"B\\\", \\\"N\\\"),\\n                          age = c(\\\"adult\\\", \\\"child\\\", \\\"elder\\\"),\\n                          disabled = FALSE,\\n                          scale = 1, ox = 0, oy = 0) {\\n  kind \\u003c- match.arg(kind)\\n  age \\u003c- match.arg(age)\\n  parts \\u003c- list()\\n\\n  # head\\n  parts[[\\\"head\\\"]] \\u003c- circle_pts(0, 1.62, 0.30)\\n\\n  if (disabled) {\\n    # Redesigned for legibility at small sizes: one large, unbroken wheel\\n    # (no small second circle to be mistaken for a stray dot), seated\\n    # directly under the torso with no gap, plus a single low footrest\\n    # peg. Fewer, bigger shapes read better than several small ones once\\n    # icons are shrunk down in a grid.\\n    parts[[\\\"torso\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(\\n      x = c(-0.30, 0.30, 0.30, -0.30),\\n      y = c(1.28, 1.28, 0.62, 0.62)\\n    )\\n    parts[[\\\"wheel\\\"]] \\u003c- circle_pts(0.00, 0.28, 0.34, n = 32)\\n    parts[[\\\"footrest\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(\\n      x = c(0.34, 0.50, 0.50, 0.34),\\n      y = c(0.02, 0.02, 0.12, 0.12)\\n    )\\n  } else {\\n    parts[[\\\"torso\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(\\n      x = c(-0.34, 0.34, 0.20, -0.20),\\n      y = c(1.30, 1.30, 0.72, 0.72)\\n    )\\n\\n    if (kind == \\\"A\\\") {           # trouser legs: two bars with a slim gap\\n      parts[[\\\"leg_l\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(x = c(-0.20, -0.03, -0.06, -0.20),\\n                                      y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\\n      parts[[\\\"leg_r\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(x = c(0.03, 0.20, 0.20, 0.06),\\n                                      y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\\n    } else if (kind == \\\"B\\\") {    # skirt\\n      parts[[\\\"legs\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(x = c(-0.20, 0.20, 0.46, -0.46),\\n                                     y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\\n    } else if (kind == \\\"N\\\") {    # half trouser (left) / half skirt (right)\\n      parts[[\\\"leg_l\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(x = c(-0.20, -0.02, -0.05, -0.20),\\n                                      y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\\n      parts[[\\\"legs_skirt_half\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(x = c(0.00, 0.20, 0.46, 0.00),\\n                                                y = c(0.72, 0.72, 0.00, 0.00))\\n    }\\n\\n    if (age == \\\"elder\\\") {\\n      parts[[\\\"cane\\\"]] \\u003c- data.frame(x = c(0.36, 0.40, 0.58, 0.54),\\n                                     y = c(0.78, 0.78, 0.02, 0.02))\\n    }\\n  }\\n\\n  # apply scale (child = smaller) then offset into the grid position\\n  out \\u003c- lapply(names(parts), function(nm) {\\n    p \\u003c- parts[[nm]]\\n    data.frame(part = nm, x = ox + scale * p$x, y = oy + scale * p$y)\\n  })\\n  do.call(rbind, out)\\n}\\n\\n# ---- composition sampling -----------------------------------------------\\n\\n#' Largest-remainder sampling: turns a named vector of proportions into\\n#' exactly `n` labels, hitting the target proportions as closely as\\n#' integer counts allow, then shuffles their order.\\nsample_counts \\u003c- function(n, props, seed) {\\n  stopifnot(\\\"`props` must have positive values\\\" = all(props > 0))\\n  props \\u003c- props / sum(props)\\n  set.seed(seed)\\n  raw \\u003c- props * n\\n  counts \\u003c- floor(raw)\\n  remainder \\u003c- n - sum(counts)\\n  if (remainder > 0) {\\n    order \\u003c- order(-(raw - counts))\\n    for (i in seq_len(remainder)) {\\n      idx \\u003c- order[((i - 1) %% length(order)) + 1]\\n      counts[idx] \\u003c- counts[idx] + 1\\n    }\\n  }\\n  sample(rep(names(props), counts))\\n}\\n\\n# ---- colour -----------------------------------------------------------\\n\\n#' Map a numeric value to a symmetric diverging colour, vivid at both\\n#' extremes and light at zero (the \\\"null effect\\\" point). `value` need\\n#' not be centred on the data -- 0 is always treated as the reference\\n#' point, so effect sizes / differences map intuitively.\\n#'\\n#' Default endpoints are blue/orange from the Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe\\n#' palette (distinguishable under deuteranopia, protanopia, and\\n#' tritanopia) rather than a red/blue or red/green diverging scale.\\ndiverging_colors \\u003c- function(value, neg = \\\"#0072B2\\\", mid = \\\"#F2F1EC\\\", pos = \\\"#E69F00\\\") {\\n  span \\u003c- max(abs(value), 1e-9)\\n  tt \\u003c- value / span                     # -1 .. 1, 0 = null\\n  ramp_lo \\u003c- grDevices::colorRamp(c(neg, mid))\\n  ramp_hi \\u003c- grDevices::colorRamp(c(mid, pos))\\n  to_hex \\u003c- function(m) grDevices::rgb(m[, 1], m[, 2], m[, 3], maxColorValue = 255)\\n  vapply(tt, function(t) {\\n    if (t \\u003c= 0) to_hex(ramp_lo(t + 1))\\n    else        to_hex(ramp_hi(t))\\n  }, character(1))\\n}\\n\\n# ---- automatic grid shape -----------------------------------------------\\n\\n#' Pick the `ncol` (icons per row) that makes an n-icon grid's bounding\\n#' box (`ncol * dx` wide by `ceiling(n / ncol) * dy` tall) match a target\\n#' width:height `aspect` ratio as closely as possible -- e.g. so the\\n#' figure fills a 16:9 slide with minimal leftover margin either way.\\nchoose_ncol \\u003c- function(n, dx, dy, aspect) {\\n  ncols \\u003c- seq_len(n)\\n  nrows \\u003c- ceiling(n / ncols)\\n  grid_ratio \\u003c- (ncols * dx) / (nrows * dy)\\n  # ## Summary of Findings

### 1. Overall repository/project structure

The repo `/Users/robertdavies/Dropbox/teaching-critical-thinking/` is a **Quarto book/slide-deck project** (an RStudio project, `.Rproj`, with `_quarto.yml`), not organized into conventional `scripts/`, `R/`, `data/` subfolders — everything sits **flat at the top level**:

- **Content chapters** (`.qmd`): e.g. `introduction.qmd`, `how-science-works.qmd`, `evaluating-evidence.qmd`, `what-is-theory.qmd`, `subjectivity-objectivity-virtues.qmd`, `lying-cheating.qmd`, `working-with-citations.qmd`, `conclusions.qmd`, `index.qmd`, etc. — these build into the Quarto "book" (output in `docs/` and `_book/`).
- **Slide deck**: `doing-being-science.qmd` (a `revealjs` presentation) — this is the one that actually **sources all five R scripts** together (lines 29–33: `person-grid.R`, `concept-map.R`, `testing-sequence.R`, `sampling-distributions.R`, `peer-review-workflow.R`) to build figures for slides on sampling/measurement/NHST.
- **Five standalone R "figure library" scripts** at top level: `person-grid.R`, `testing-sequence.R`, `sampling-distributions.R`, `concept-map.R`, `peer-review-workflow.R`.
- **Matching "walkthrough" documentation `.qmd` files**, one per script: `person-grid-walkthrough.qmd`, `testing-sequence-walkthrough.qmd`, `sampling-distributions-walkthrough.qmd`, `concept-map-walkthrough.qmd`, `peer-review-workflow-walkthrough.qmd` (each with rendered `.html` and a `_files/` folder of cached figure PNGs/libs) — these are self-contained tutorials demonstrating/testing each script in isolation.
- **Draft/synthetic-data analysis `.qmd` files** related to a different (but related) strand of work: `simulation-pipeline-tutorial-aims-1-2.qmd`, `synthetic-data-analyses-power-error-replication-aims-1-2-draft.qmd`, `-reportable.qmd`, `synthetic-data-power-error-replication-effect-size-sampling-draft-development.qmd`/`-draft-review.qmd`.
- **Documentation/process notes**: two long markdown "conversation logs" — `critical-thinking-script-documentation-conversation.md` and `testing-sequence_sampling-distribution_concept-map_figure-scripts.md` — recording the iterative design/debugging dialogue that produced these scripts (useful provenance: shows earlier, buggier versions of `testing-sequence.R`/`sampling-distributions.R`/`person-grid.R` and the fixes applied).
- **Assets**: `files/`, `docs/files/` (screenshots for a "how to set up the book" workflow), many standalone `.png`/`.jpg` figures copied from published papers (e.g. `Wieczorek-2021-fig-2-...png`), `references.bib`, `psychological-bulletin.csl`.
- **Build artifacts**: `_book/`, `docs/` (GitHub Pages output), `.quarto/` (cache/freeze/xref), `*_files/` folders per rendered qmd, `.Rproj.user/`.
- No `R/`, `scripts/`, `data/`, or `figures/` subfolders exist; organization is **by topic/chapter at the root**, with the 5 figure-generation scripts functioning as a shared "helper library" sourced into chapters as needed, each documented by its own walkthrough `.qmd`.

### 2. The five R scripts

All five share a strict format: a `#'` roxygen-style block header (file name, purpose, model/geometry description, dependency/sourcing order, a "Quarto usage" fenced R-chunk example), then `library(ggplot2)`, then roxygen-documented functions. All build base ggplot2 figures (polygons/curves/points) for the `doing-being-science.qmd` slide deck, illustrating the logic of psychological testing → sampling → sampling distributions → NHST.

- **`person-grid.R`** (280 lines): Core/base library. Generates a parametrized "restroom-sign" pictogram of people as polygons (head/torso/legs/wheelchair/cane), with `person_parts()` building one icon and `person_grid()` laying out an n-icon grid. Two color "modes": `"diversity"` (sampled skin tones, via helper `sample_counts()` — largest-remainder apportionment of silhouette kind/age/disability proportions) or `"value"` (continuous diverging colour scale via `diverging_colors()`, Okabe-Ito colourblind-safe blue/white/orange, 0 = null). Has `choose_ncol()` to auto-pick grid shape matching slide aspect ratio. Returns `list(plot, data, meta, alt_text)` — notably auto-generates **alt text** for accessibility. This is the dependency that `testing-sequence.R` and `peer-review-workflow.R` build on (`person_parts()`, `sample_counts()`, `diverging_colors()` are reused).

- **`testing-sequence.R`** (214 lines): Extends `person-grid.R` with a composite "person at a computer" icon (`monitor_parts()` + `person_at_computer()`), illustrating "one person tested → two people tested → a whole sample tested." `testing_icons(n, scores=...)` draws n icons, optionally labelling each with its score (`x = <score>`) for n=1/2 steps, or an unlabelled grid for the "sample" step. Supports same diversity/value colour modes as person-grid. `testing_icons_studies()` facets multiple independent study samples side by side (icon analogue of `sampling-distributions.R`'s histogram/dotpile grids). Requires `person-grid.R` sourced first.

- **`sampling-distributions.R`** (434 lines, most complex/statistical): Simulates vocabulary-test scores from a **trial level up** psychometric (IRT-like) model: `theta_i ~ N(theta_mu, theta_sigma)` (ability, logit scale) → `p_i = plogis(theta_i)` → 40 Bernoulli item responses → `observed_score = sum` (binomial, naturally bounded [0,40], no post-hoc clipping needed — an improvement noted in the dev-conversation log over an earlier CTT version that clipped/rounded continuous scores). `calibrate_ability()` numerically solves (via `integrate()`/`uniroot()`) for `theta_mu`/`theta_sigma` so the emergent mean matches `mu` and emergent reliability (or directly `sd_true`) matches a target — mirrors real test theory (mean, reliability, spread aren't independently free). Handles measurement-error attenuation of correlations (`corr(observed, true ability) = sqrt(reliability)`) when inducing `r_with_x`. Core simulators: `simulate_vocab_data()`, `simulate_studies()` (independent samples for "repeated studies" figure), `simulate_parallel_forms()` (test-retest/parallel-forms check of reliability). Figures: `plot_dots()` (1-2 scores on a line), `plot_dotpile()` (ggdist::stat_dots "pile of dots" — distribution as discrete points, not smoothed density), `plot_dotpile_grid()`/`plot_histogram_grid()` (faceted by `study`, for sampling-variability-across-studies demonstrations, directly supporting NHST/sampling-distribution concepts), `plot_histogram()`, `plot_scatter()` (with `geom_smooth(method="lm")`). Requires `ggplot2` + `ggdist`.

- **`concept-map.R`** (221 lines): A generic, domain-independent "N columns of ellipses with many-to-many curved links between adjacent columns" diagram generator, styled after McElreath's *Statistical Rethinking* Fig 1.2 (theories → process models → statistical models). `concept_map(columns, edges, titles, ...)` builds ellipse polygons (`ellipse_pts()`) and `geom_curve()` edges with heavy input validation (checks `dx` spacing sufficiency, out-of-range edge indices with informative error messages naming the offending column/index). Unlike the other four, it's about theory/measurement mapping, not directly about sampling/testing mechanics, but is used in the same slide deck (used for "the theory is not the hypothesis" slide per the dev log) and shares the same aesthetic/coding conventions.

- **`peer-review-workflow.R`** (144 lines): A single fixed flow-diagram of the author→editor→2 reviewers→editor→author peer-review cycle, reusing `person_at_computer()` from `testing-sequence.R` (so depends on both `person-grid.R` and `testing-sequence.R` being sourced first). Uses `geom_segment`/`geom_curve` arrows (fan-out to two reviewers, fan-in back, a dashed "reject → revise & resubmit → repeat" loop-back arrow), role/step-caption text annotations. Thematically about the publication/evaluation process rather than sampling/NHST per se, but visually integrated into the same icon "aesthetic family."

### 3. Shared conventions across the scripts

- **Header block**: every file begins with a `#' ====...====` banner comment giving the filename, a prose description of what it does/models, explicit **sourcing/dependency requirements** ("Requires X.R sourced first (same folder)"), and a fenced ```` ```{r} ```` **"Quarto usage"** example block showing realistic calls — effectively doubling as both documentation and informal runnable examples.
- **roxygen-style (`#'`) function docs** with `@param`/`@return` tags throughout, even though these aren't a formal R package (no `DESCRIPTION`/`NAMESPACE`) — roxygen conventions used purely for human-readable documentation.
- **`library(ggplot2)`** at top of every file; `sampling-distributions.R` additionally uses `ggdist::stat_dots` (namespaced call, with `requireNamespace()` guard + informative `stop()` if missing, rather than `library(ggdist)`).
- **`set.seed(seed)` reproducibility pattern**: functions take an explicit `seed` argument (default usually 1), and internally call `set.seed()` (sometimes offsetting it, e.g. `seed+1`, `seed+2`, `seed+3`, to decorrelate kind/age/disability/colour sampling draws) rather than relying on global RNG state.
- **Consistent colour palette / identity scale**: hex colours used directly with `scale_fill_identity()`; a shared blue (`#3B6EA5`) is the default "researcher"/data colour across scripts; Okabe-Ito colourblind-safe diverging palette (`#0072B2`/`#F2F1EC`/`#E69F00`) used for "value" mode.
- **Functions return `list(plot = ..., data = ...)`** (sometimes plus `meta`, `alt_text`, `edges`/`nodes`) rather than a bare ggplot object — lets a caller both display the figure and inspect/reuse underlying data.
- **`theme_void()` / `theme_minimal()`** consistently used (no default ggplot grey theme), with explicit `coord_equal()` for icon-based plots.
