Useful as a structural\n  template (DGP function → fitting/diagnosis helpers → sweep grid → orchestrator →\n  summarize → visualize; parameter table grounded in real estimates; draft-with-code\n  vs. reportable-without-code pairing) but far heavier machinery than appropriate for\n  a teaching script meant to run live/inline.\n- **New grounding source supplied by the user**: Vermeiren, Vandendaele & Brysbaert\n  (2023, *Behavior Research Methods*), \"Validated tests for language research with\n  university students...\" This gives empirically grounded parameters for a *battery*\n  of four correlated tests to simulate:\n    - **StuVoc1** (specialized-word vocabulary test): 50 items, 4-alternative forced\n      choice (4AFC), \u003ccite index=\"22-0\">\"Figure 12 First panel: Distribution of sum scores (mean=32.3, SD=8.36) on StuVoc1 based on 577 participants\"\u003c/cite>, reliability\n      alpha/ICC/split-half/omega3/omega-h = \u003ccite index=\"22-0\">\".88 .86 .87 .88 .69\"\u003c/cite>.\n    - **StuVoc2** (general-word, parallel-form vocabulary test): 50 items, 4AFC,\n      \u003ccite index=\"23-0\">\"Distribution of sum scores on StuVoc2 (mean 34.0, SD=9.43)\"\u003c/cite>, reliability\n      \u003ccite index=\"23-0\">\".91 .90 .89 .91 .68\"\u003c/cite> (alpha/ICC/split-half/omega3/omega-h). In Study 5 it\n      correlated \u003ccite index=\"17-0\">\"strong correlation of .82 between Voc1 specialized and Voc2 general\"\u003c/cite>.\n    - **GK** (general-knowledge test): 65 items, 4AFC, \u003ccite index=\"24-0\">\"Distribution of sum scores on the general knowledge test (mean=42.2, SD=7.95)\"\u003c/cite>, reliability\n      \u003ccite index=\"24-0\">\".83 .79 .82 .81 .43\"\u003c/cite>; correlates with StuVoc1 at \u003ccite index=\"22-0\">\"GK (n =378) .67\"\u003c/cite>.\n    - **ART3** (Author Recognition Test): 60 real fiction-author names + 30 foil\n      (non-author) names; participant responds yes/no per name — a genuine\n      **signal-detection task** with real false positives (saying \"yes\" to a foil)\n      and false negatives (saying \"no\" to a real author), not a 4AFC accuracy item.\n      \u003ccite index=\"25-0\">\"Distributions of sum scores on ART3 (mean=57.1, SD=9.31)\"\u003c/cite>, reliability\n      \u003ccite index=\"25-0\">\".9 .88 .87 .44\"\u003c/cite> (alpha/ICC/omega3/omega-h); correlates with StuVoc1 at\n      \u003ccite index=\"22-0\">\"ART (n=378) .52\"\u003c/cite>.\n    - All four load on a single **crystallized intelligence** latent factor in\n      Vermeiren et al.'s SEM (Study 5, Fig. 11), alongside reading comprehension\n      (which the user has not asked to include).\n    - The paper's own power-analysis illustration (Fig. 1, \"Power considerations\")\n      is a near-perfect template for concept area (2): \u003ccite index=\"3-7,4-0\">\"Figure 1 shows the results one can expect if such a Pearson correlation between two normally distributed variables is investigated with sample sizes from N=40 to N=400... Each dot represents the outcome of a single 'study' (for a total of 2000 studies)... For study samples of N=40, only one quarter of the studies are expected to result in a significant correlation... A formal power analysis indicates that the chances of observing a significant correlation are only .23 and the probability of observing a (nonsignificant) correlation opposite to the one known to be true is .11. Sample sizes of N=200... chance of .81 to observe a significant correlation, and a 99.8% chance of a correlation in the right direction\"\u003c/cite>. This gives concrete target numbers (power ≈ .23 at N=40, ≈.81 at N=200, for a true r=.2) that a teaching simulation can be checked against.\n\n## 3. Core design decision: a shared, calibrated multi-test DGP\n\nRather than four unrelated simulators, build **one shared data-generating process**\nthat produces a person's scores on all four tests at once, reproducing (a) each\ntest's marginal distribution/reliability and (b) the inter-test correlation\nstructure, by routing each test's \"true ability\" through a single latent\ncrystallized-intelligence factor — mirroring Vermeiren's own SEM result rather than\nsimulating each test in isolation.\n\n**Person-level structure** (one row per simulated participant):\n\n- `g_i ~ N(0, 1)` — latent crystallized intelligence (unobserved).\n- For each test *t* ∈ {StuVoc1, StuVoc2, GK, ART3}: a true ability\n  `theta_t_i = lambda_t * g_i + sqrt(1 - lambda_t^2) * u_t_i`, `u_t_i ~ N(0,1)`\n  independent across tests and people — i.e. a one-factor model with test-specific\n  loadings `lambda_t`. Loadings are solved numerically (`uniroot()`/closed-form,\n  mirroring the existing `calibrate_ability()` pattern in `sampling-distributions.R`)\n  so that the *emergent* pairwise correlations between simulated summed scores match\n  the Vermeiren Study 5 values above (StuVoc1–StuVoc2 ≈ .82, StuVoc1–GK ≈ .67,\n  StuVoc1–ART3 ≈ .52; GK–ART3 and StuVoc2–GK/ART3 taken from Table 8 of the paper for\n  consistency, with a documented note that this is a single-factor simplification of\n  Vermeiren's true multi-factor SEM).\n\n**Item-level structure** (two distinct response-generating mechanisms, both needed\nfor the error-rate work in concept area 3):\n\n- **4AFC accuracy items** (StuVoc1, StuVoc2, GK): item difficulty `b_j`, a\n  Rasch/2PL-style correct-response probability with a **guessing floor** appropriate\n  to 4 alternatives, `p_ij = 0.25 + 0.75 * plogis(a * (theta_t_i - b_j))`\n  (discrimination `a` fixed or test-specific), `response_ij ~ Bernoulli(p_ij)`,\n  summed score `= sum_j response_ij` (naturally bounded, as in the existing\n  `sampling-distributions.R` approach — no post-hoc clipping needed). Item\n  difficulties `b_j` drawn so that the test's mean/SD/reliability hit the targets\n  above, again via a calibration helper.\n- **Signal-detection recognition items** (ART3): separate item pools of 60 \"author\"\n  and 30 \"foil\" names. Person's sensitivity to each pool is driven by `theta_ART3_i`\n  (criterion fixed or allowed to vary); hit rate `P(yes | author)` and false-alarm\n  rate `P(yes | foil)` follow a simple signal-detection model (e.g. `d'`/criterion\n  parameterization or a logistic equivalent) so that both the overall summed score\n  AND a per-person **false-positive rate** (yes-to-foil proportion) and **false-\n  negative rate** (no-to-author proportion) are directly simulated and inspectable.\n  This becomes the concrete anchor for concept area 3 — a real false-positive/\n  false-negative rate at the item level — before the walkthrough generalizes the\n  same language to NHST decisions at the study level.\n\nThis shared DGP lives in one sourced helper script (proposed name\n`psych-battery-dgp.R`) analogous to how `person-grid.R` is sourced by\n`testing-sequence.R`/`peer-review-workflow.R`. All three concept-area scripts source\nit rather than duplicating simulation code.\n\n**Calibration/validation step** (to be run once, shown in the shared script's\nwalkthrough): simulate a large one-off sample, recompute mean/SD/reliability per\ntest and the inter-test correlation matrix, and compare against the Vermeiren\nTable 6/7/8 target values in a small table — directly mirroring how the Aims-1–2\nwork grounded its DGP in real fitted-model estimates.\n\n## 4. Proposed script set (4 new files + 4 walkthroughs)\n\n| Script | Concept area | What it does |\n|---|---|---|\n| `psych-battery-dgp.R` | shared infrastructure | Latent-factor + per-test ability generation; 4AFC item-response simulator; ART3 signal-detection simulator; `simulate_battery(n, seed, ...)` returning person-level summed scores (+ optionally item-level long data); calibration helpers to solve for loadings/difficulties against target reliability/correlations; a validation table/plot comparing simulated vs. target statistics. No plots of its own beyond the validation check (or a minimal score-distribution plot reusing `sampling-distributions.R`'s `plot_dotpile()`/`plot_histogram()` where applicable). |\n| `sampling-measurement-error.R` | (1) sampling & measurement error, sampling distributions | Sources `psych-battery-dgp.R`. Demonstrates: (a) measurement error for one test — repeated *parallel-form* simulation (StuVoc1 vs. StuVoc2 as \"two forms\" of the same ability) showing test-retest/parallel-forms scatter and how reliability limits agreement; (b) sampling error — repeatedly draw independent samples of size *N* and look at the distribution of the sample mean and sample correlation (StuVoc1–GK) across samples, i.e. a sampling distribution; (c) an explicit side-by-side figure distinguishing \"one person's score has measurement error\" from \"one study's estimate has sampling error,\" extending the icon-sequence idea already piloted in `testing-sequence.R`/`sampling-distributions.R` but now for a correlation, not just a single test score. |\n| `nhst-power.R` | (2) NHST and power | Sources `psych-battery-dgp.R`. Core decision: test `H0: r(StuVoc1, GK) = 0` (also offer a two-group mean-difference variant using a simulated \"intervention\" subgroup, if wanted) via `cor.test()`/`t.test()`; (a) a direct replication-in-miniature of Vermeiren's Fig. 1 \"corridor\" plot (N from ~40–400, many simulated studies per N, points coloured/shaped by significance), validated against their reported power ≈ .23 @ N=40 and ≈ .81 @ N=200 for a *true r = .2* benchmark case, then repeated at the *true* StuVoc1–GK population correlation (~.67) for the main teaching example; (b) a power curve sweeping N at several true effect sizes (0, .2, .67 among others), with the r=0 curve kept visually distinct as the Type I error rate; (c) short NHST walkthrough of a single simulated study (CI, p-value, decision) tied back to the long-run frequency interpretation. |\n| `error-rates-process-control.R` | (3) false positive/negative rates as Neyman–Pearson process-control error rates | Sources `psych-battery-dgp.R`. Two-part structure: (a) **concrete anchor** — ART3's item-level signal-detection simulation directly yields a per-person false-positive rate (yes-to-foil) and false-negative rate (no-to-author); visualize the distribution of these rates across simulated participants, and show how a \"pass/fail\" classification rule (e.g., \"recognizes ≥ k authors\") has its own false-positive/negative rate as a *property of the rule*, not of any one application of it; (b) **abstraction to NHST** — reuse `nhst-power.R`'s `H0: r = 0` decision rule under a fixed-alpha, fixed-sample-size \"testing procedure,\" run many independent hypothetical replications under both a true-null and a true-effect world, and report the empirical long-run Type I and Type II rates as *process-control error rates* in the Neyman–Pearson sense (a property of the decision procedure applied repeatedly, contrasted explicitly with \"the evidential strength of this particular result,\" echoing Neyman & Pearson's framing and distinguishing it from Fisherian single-study p-value interpretation). |\n\nEach of the three concept-area scripts is deliberately kept \"thin\" — they orchestrate\ncalls into `psych-battery-dgp.R` plus `ggplot2` visualization/summary code — so the\nsimulation logic is written once and the pedagogical scripts stay readable.\n\n## 5. Documentation plan\n\nOne `\u003cscript>-walkthrough.qmd` per script (4 total), following the established\ntemplate exactly:\n\n- YAML header (`title`, `subtitle: \"Walkthrough: ...\"`, `toc: true`).\n- **Aims** + 3 \"After working through this, you should be able to...\" learning\n  objectives.\n- **Prerequisites/assumptions**: packages (`ggplot2`, base R `stats` for\n  `cor.test`/`t.test`/`uniroot`; no new heavy dependencies expected), sourcing order\n  (`psych-battery-dgp.R` first for the three concept scripts), reader background.\n- **How it works**: prose + a small Mermaid flowchart per script (e.g. for the DGP:\n  latent factor → per-test true ability → item responses → summed score; for\n  NHST/power: generate sample → fit test → classify significant/not → repeat →\n  summarize).\n- **Element-by-element walkthrough**: one function per subsection, `.callout-note`\n  asides for non-obvious design choices (e.g., why a guessing floor matters for 4AFC\n  items; the loading-calibration `uniroot()` call; the Vermeiren-Fig-1\n  replication plotting code), and a runnable demo chunk.\n- **Quarto usage / integration**: standalone usage snippet; **Parameter quick\n  reference** table; **Common errors** table (sourced from the script's actual\n  `stopifnot()`/`warning()` text).\n- **Exercises** (3–5 per doc, e.g. \"re-run the power sweep for the StuVoc1–ART3\n  correlation (r≈.52) instead of StuVoc1–GK and compare the N needed for 80% power\").\n- **See also**: cross-links between the four docs and to `sampling-distributions-walkthrough.qmd`\n  (as prior art for the single-test case).\n- Each `.qmd` renders standalone (own YAML, own `source()` calls); Scope, weight, and integration (proposed defaults — flagged for confirmation)\n\n- **Standalone scripts + walkthroughs only.** Not wired into `doing-being-science.qmd`\n  for this pass (that deck is about the icon/figure sequence; these scripts are\n  about inferential-statistics demonstrations with tables/plots, a different\n  register). Can be revisited later if the user wants slide integration.\n- **Lightweight/fast simulation**, matching the pedagogical (not research) purpose:\n  base R + `ggplot2`, no `furrr`/background jobs/`.rds` caching infrastructure.\n  Default replicate counts: hundreds to a couple thousand simulated studies per\n  sample-size/effect-size cell for the power sweeps (enough to get reasonably stable\n  power estimates and to visually reproduce Vermeiren's Fig. 1 scatter), chosen so\n  each script's demo chunks run in low single-digit seconds and the full walkthrough\n  renders in well under a minute. <div><tool-result call-id="toolu_017gugwWFbwH31E5jv18VfoT"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 27.0KB, 567 lines, showing lines 1-464 (output byte budget reached)]\n1\t#' =========...[truncated, total 24515 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 27.0KB, 567 lines, showing lines 1-464 (output byte budget reached)]\n#' ============================================================\n#' psych-battery-dgp.R\n#'\n#' Shared data-generating process (DGP) and diagnostic/sweep engine for a\n#' simulated battery of four correlated psychological tests, grounded in\n#' Vermeiren, Vandendaele & Brysbaert (2023, Behavior Research Methods):\n#'\n#'   - StuVoc1  specialized-word vocabulary test, 50 items, 4AFC\n#'   - StuVoc2  general-word vocabulary test (parallel form), 50 items, 4AFC\n#'   - GK       general-knowledge test, 65 items, 4AFC\n#'   - ART3     author recognition test, 60 real-author + 30 foil names,\n#'              yes/no recognition (not 4AFC)\n#'\n#' Every simulated participant completes every test (fully crossed, no\n#' missingness). Three things are independently controllable, matching\n#' the three \"dials\" this battery is meant to teach with:\n#'\n#'   (i)   participant sample size (`n`)\n#'   (ii)  measurement error, via a per-test `reliability`\n#'   (iii) the *true* (construct-level, disattenuated) correlation between\n#'         tests' underlying abilities, which -- together with (ii) --\n#'         determines how strong a correlation the *observed* test scores\n#'         will show (classical test theory attenuation: observed\n#'         correlation = true correlation * sqrt(reliability_x * reliability_y))\n#'\n#' Design (trial/item level up, as in sampling-distributions.R, so every\n#' simulated score is *structurally* bounded -- no clipping anywhere):\n#'\n#'   Standardized true ability (correlated across tests):\n#'     z_i ~ MVN(0, Sigma_true)     (one row per person, one column per test)\n#'   Per test t, calibrated location/scale (see calibrate_ability_general()):\n#'     theta_ti   = theta_mu_t + theta_sigma_t * z_it\n#'     p_ti       = guessing_t + (1 - guessing_t) * plogis(theta_ti)\n#'   4AFC tests (StuVoc1, StuVoc2, GK):\n#'     score_ti   ~ Binomial(n_items_t, p_ti)\n#'   ART3 (60 author + 30 foil items, no guessing floor):\n#'     hits_i             ~ Binomial(60, p_ART3,i)   -- correct \"yes\" to an author\n#'     correct_rejects_i  ~ Binomial(30, p_ART3,i)   -- correct \"no\" to a foil\n#'     score_ART3,i       =  hits_i + correct_rejects_i\n#'     false_negative_rate_i = 1 - hits_i / 60   (said \"no\" to a real author)\n#'     false_positive_rate_i = 1 - correct_rejects_i / 30 (said \"yes\" to a foil)\n#'\n#' `reliability` and `Sigma_true` aren't set directly on the observed-score\n#' scale -- `calibrate_ability_general()` solves each test's ability\n#' location/scale numerically so its *emergent* reliability matches the\n#' target, and `build_sigma_true()` converts a target *observed*-score\n#' correlation matrix into the *true*-score (disattenuated) correlation\n#' matrix that actually needs to be fed to the multivariate draw, via\n#' r_true = r_observed / sqrt(reliability_x * reliability_y). This mirrors\n#' real test theory: you cannot set reliability, true correlation, and\n#' observed correlation all independently -- fixing any two determines the\n#' third.\n#'\n#' A generic sweep/diagnostic engine (`run_sweep()` / `summarize_sweep()`)\n#' repeatedly draws a dataset, runs a correlation test on a chosen pair of\n#' tests, and classifies the result (significant? correct sign? CI covers\n#' the truth?) -- the same pattern used in the project's heavier Aims 1-2\n#' simulation work, scaled down to run inline rather than as a background\n#' job.\n#'\n#' Requires: ggplot2, MASS (called via `::` only, so it never masks\n#' dplyr::select()), dplyr, tidyr, purrr.\n#'\n#' Quarto usage:\n#'   ```{r}\n#'   source(\"psych-battery-dgp.R\")\n#'   d \u003c- simulate_battery(n = 500, seed = 1)\n#'   cor(d[c(\"StuVoc1\", \"StuVoc2\", \"GK\", \"ART3\")])\n#'   sweep \u003c- run_sweep(n_grid = c(40, 100, 200), true_corr_grid = c(0, 0.2, 0.67),\n#'                       reps = 200, seed_base = 42)\n#'   plot_power_heatmap(summarize_sweep(sweep))\n#'   ```\n#' ============================================================\n\nlibrary(ggplot2)\n\n# ---- test specifications (Vermeiren et al. 2023, Study 5 defaults) --------\n\n#' Item counts, target mean, and guessing floor for each test. `mu` and\n#' `n_items` are taken from Vermeiren et al.'s Study 5 (Table 6 for the\n#' vocabulary/GK tests, Fig. 16 for ART3); `guessing = 0.25` reflects the\n#' 4-alternative-forced-choice format of StuVoc1/StuVoc2/GK, and\n#' `guessing = 0` reflects that ART3 is a yes/no recognition task, not 4AFC.\ndefault_test_specs \u003c- function() {\n  list(\n    StuVoc1 = list(n_items = 50, mu = 32.3, guessing = 0.25),\n    StuVoc2 = list(n_items = 50, mu = 34.0, guessing = 0.25),\n    GK      = list(n_items = 65, mu = 42.2, guessing = 0.25),\n    ART3    = list(n_items = 90, mu = 57.1, guessing = 0.00, split = c(authors = 60, foils = 30))\n  )\n}\n\n#' Default per-test reliability (Vermeiren et al. 2023, Study 5: alpha for\n#' StuVoc1/StuVoc2/GK, alpha for ART3 -- see Table 6 and Fig. 16).\ndefault_reliability_vec \u003c- function() {\n  c(StuVoc1 = 0.88, StuVoc2 = 0.91, GK = 0.83, ART3 = 0.90)\n}\n\n#' Default target *observed*-score correlation matrix between tests\n#' (Vermeiren et al. 2023, Study 5, Tables 7-8 / Fig. 12): this is what the\n#' simulated *summed scores* should correlate at when reliability is left\n#' at its default -- not the latent/true-score correlation, which is\n#' recovered internally via `build_sigma_true()`.\ndefault_r_obs_matrix \u003c- function() {\n  nm \u003c- c(\"StuVoc1\", \"StuVoc2\", \"GK\", \"ART3\")\n  m \u003c- matrix(c(\n    1.00, 0.82, 0.67, 0.52,\n    0.82, 1.00, 0.71, 0.40,\n    0.67, 0.71, 1.00, 0.31,\n    0.52, 0.40, 0.31, 1.00\n  ), nrow = 4, dimnames = list(nm, nm))\n  m\n}\n\n# ---- calibration (generalizes sampling-distributions.R's calibrate_ability()) --\n\n#' Expectation of `f(theta)` under theta ~ N(theta_mu, theta_sigma), by\n#' numerical integration (same device as sampling-distributions.R).\nexpect_theta \u003c- function(f, theta_mu, theta_sigma) {\n  integrate(function(theta) f(theta) * dnorm(theta, theta_mu, theta_sigma),\n            lower = theta_mu - 10 * theta_sigma,\n            upper = theta_mu + 10 * theta_sigma)$value\n}\n\n#' Moments of the observed score implied by (theta_mu, theta_sigma,\n#' n_items, guessing). Generalizes sampling-distributions.R's\n#' implied_moments() with a guessing floor: p = guessing + (1-guessing) *\n#' plogis(theta), which collapses to the original model when guessing = 0.\nimplied_moments_general \u003c- function(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items, guessing = 0) {\n  p_fun  \u003c- function(th) guessing + (1 - guessing) * plogis(th)\n  p_bar  \u003c- expect_theta(p_fun, theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n  p2_bar \u003c- expect_theta(function(th) p_fun(th)^2, theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n  pq_bar \u003c- expect_theta(function(th) { p \u003c- p_fun(th); p * (1 - p) }, theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n\n  mean_score  \u003c- n_items * p_bar\n  var_true    \u003c- n_items^2 * (p2_bar - p_bar^2)\n  var_error   \u003c- n_items * pq_bar\n  reliability \u003c- var_true / (var_true + var_error)\n\n  list(mean_score = mean_score, var_true = var_true, var_error = var_error,\n       reliability = reliability, sd_true = sqrt(var_true),\n       sd_total = sqrt(var_true + var_error))\n}\n\n#' Solve for (theta_mu, theta_sigma) so the trial-level model's emergent\n#' mean score matches `mu` and its emergent reliability matches\n#' `reliability`, for a test with `n_items` items and a `guessing` floor.\n#' Same robust nested-uniroot pattern as sampling-distributions.R's\n#' calibrate_ability(): an outer search over theta_sigma, an inner search\n#' over theta_mu, with the outer bracket doubled until it contains a root\n#' and an informative error if the target isn't achievable.\ncalibrate_ability_general \u003c- function(mu, reliability = 0.80, n_items = 40, guessing = 0) {\n  floor_score \u003c- guessing * n_items\n  stopifnot(\n    \"`mu` must be strictly between `guessing * n_items` and `n_items`\" =\n      mu > floor_score && mu \u003c n_items,\n    \"`reliability` must be strictly between 0 and 1\" =\n      reliability > 0 && reliability \u003c 1\n  )\n\n  theta_mu_for_sigma \u003c- function(theta_sigma) {\n    uniroot(function(theta_mu) implied_moments_general(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items, guessing)$mean_score - mu,\n            lower = -15, upper = 15, extendInt = \"yes\")$root\n  }\n\n  reliability_gap \u003c- function(theta_sigma) {\n    theta_mu \u003c- theta_mu_for_sigma(theta_sigma)\n    implied_moments_general(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items, guessing)$reliability - reliability\n  }\n  gap_at \u003c- function(theta_sigma) tryCatch(reliability_gap(theta_sigma), error = function(e) NA_real_)\n  lower \u003c- 0.02\n  upper \u003c- 8\n  max_upper \u003c- 128\n  g \u003c- gap_at(upper)\n  while ((is.na(g) || g \u003c 0) && upper \u003c max_upper) {\n    upper \u003c- upper * 2\n    g \u003c- gap_at(upper)\n  }\n  fail_message \u003c- sprintf(\n    paste(\"reliability = %.3f is not achievable at mu = %.1f with n_items = %d\",\n          \"and guessing = %.2f (it would require an implausibly large,\",\n          \"numerically unstable ability spread). Try a lower reliability\",\n          \"(\u003c= ~0.99 is usually safe), a larger n_items, or a mu further\",\n          \"from the guessing floor.\"),\n    reliability, mu, n_items, guessing\n  )\n  if (is.na(g) || g \u003c 0) stop(fail_message)\n  theta_sigma \u003c- tryCatch(uniroot(reliability_gap, lower = lower, upper = upper)$root,\n                           error = function(e) stop(fail_message))\n  theta_mu \u003c- theta_mu_for_sigma(theta_sigma)\n  list(theta_mu = theta_mu, theta_sigma = theta_sigma,\n       moments = implied_moments_general(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items, guessing))\n}\n\n# A sweep calls calibrate_ability_general() with the same (mu, reliability,\n# n_items, guessing) many times over (reliability/n don't change within a\n# cell's replicates); cache by rounded arguments so repeated calls in a\n# sweep are near-instant instead of re-running uniroot()/integrate().\n.calibration_cache \u003c- new.env(parent = emptyenv())\nget_calibration \u003c- function(mu, reliability, n_items, guessing = 0) {\n  key \u003c- sprintf(\"mu=%.4f|rel=%.5f|n=%d|g=%.3f\", mu, reliability, n_items, guessing)\n  if (is.null(.calibration_cache[[key]])) {\n    .calibration_cache[[key]] \u003c- calibrate_ability_general(mu, reliability, n_items, guessing)\n  }\n  .calibration_cache[[key]]\n}\n\n# ---- true-score correlation matrix (attenuation) ---------------------------\n\n#' Disattenuated (true-score) correlation implied by a target *observed*\n#' correlation and the two tests' reliabilities: r_true = r_obs /\n#' sqrt(rel_x * rel_y). This is the classical test theory \"correction for\n#' attenuation\" formula, applied in reverse of its usual use (normally used\n#' to estimate a disattenuated correlation from data; here used to find the\n#' latent correlation that will *produce* a target observed correlation\n#' once measurement error is added back in).\ndisattenuate \u003c- function(r_obs, reliability_x, reliability_y) {\n  denom \u003c- sqrt(reliability_x * reliability_y)\n  r_true \u003c- r_obs / denom\n  if (abs(r_true) > 1) {\n    warning(sprintf(\n      paste(\"Target observed correlation r = %.2f is not achievable at\",\n            \"reliabilities %.2f and %.2f (it would require a true-score\",\n            \"correlation above 1); capping the true-score correlation at\",\n            \"%.3f.\"),\n      r_obs, reliability_x, reliability_y, sign(r_true) * 0.999\n    ))\n    r_true \u003c- sign(r_true) * 0.999\n  }\n  r_true\n}\n\n#' Build the 4x4 true-score (latent) correlation matrix to feed to\n#' MASS::mvrnorm(), from a target *observed*-score correlation matrix and a\n#' named vector of per-test reliabilities. If the resulting matrix isn't\n#' positive-definite (possible after capping individual cells, or after\n#' overriding a single pair of tests in a sweep), it's nudged to the\n#' nearest valid correlation matrix by eigenvalue clipping, with a warning.\nbuild_sigma_true \u003c- function(r_obs_matrix, reliability) {\n  nm \u003c- colnames(r_obs_matrix)\n  stopifnot(\n    \"`r_obs_matrix` must be named on both dimensions\" = !is.null(nm),\n    \"`reliability` must have an entry for every test in `r_obs_matrix`\" =\n      all(nm %in% names(reliability))\n  )\n  Sigma \u003c- diag(length(nm))\n  dimnames(Sigma) \u003c- list(nm, nm)\n  for (i in seq_along(nm)) {\n    for (j in seq_along(nm)) {\n      if (i == j) next\n      Sigma[i, j] \u003c- disattenuate(r_obs_matrix[nm[i], nm[j]], reliability[[nm[i]]], reliability[[nm[j]]])\n    }\n  }\n  ev \u003c- eigen(Sigma, symmetric = TRUE)\n  if (any(ev$values \u003c 1e-8)) {\n    warning(\"Sigma_true was not positive-definite after disattenuation; nudging to the nearest valid correlation matrix (eigenvalue clipping).\")\n    vals \u003c- pmax(ev$values, 1e-6)\n    adj \u003c- ev$vectors %*% diag(vals) %*% t(ev$vectors)\n    d \u003c- sqrt(diag(adj))\n    Sigma \u003c- adj / outer(d, d)\n    dimnames(Sigma) \u003c- list(nm, nm)\n  }\n  Sigma\n}\n\n# ---- simulation -------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Simulate one study: `n` participants' scores on all four tests.\n#'\n#' @param n              sample size.\n#' @param reliability    named list/vector overriding one or more tests'\n#'                        reliability (default: `default_reliability_vec()`).\n#'                        Dial (ii) -- measurement error.\n#' @param Sigma_true      a 4x4 named true-score correlation matrix (as\n#'                        produced by `build_sigma_true()`). If NULL\n#'                        (default), it's built from\n#'                        `default_r_obs_matrix()` and whatever\n#'                        `reliability` is in effect, so the *observed*\n#'                        scores land near the Vermeiren-default\n#'                        correlations unless overridden. Dial (iii) --\n#'                        true/construct-level correlation.\n#' @param seed           for reproducibility.\n#' @param keep_latent    if TRUE, also return each test's `_theta`\n#'                        (ability, logit scale) and `_p` (per-item\n#'                        probability) columns -- useful for directly\n#'                        showing measurement error (true theta vs.\n#'                        observed score).\n#' @return a data frame: `id`, one score column per test (`StuVoc1`,\n#'   `StuVoc2`, `GK`, `ART3`), plus `ART3_fp_rate`/`ART3_fn_rate` (per-\n#'   person false-positive/false-negative rates on the recognition task).\nsimulate_battery \u003c- function(n, reliability = NULL, Sigma_true = NULL, seed = NULL, keep_latent = FALSE) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  specs \u003c- default_test_specs()\n  rel \u003c- as.list(default_reliability_vec())\n  if (!is.null(reliability)) {\n    stopifnot(\"`reliability` names must be a subset of the four test names\" =\n                all(names(reliability) %in% names(rel)))\n    rel[names(reliability)] \u003c- as.list(reliability)\n  }\n  if (is.null(Sigma_true)) {\n    Sigma_true \u003c- build_sigma_true(default_r_obs_matrix(), rel)\n  }\n  stopifnot(\n    \"`Sigma_true` must be a 4x4 matrix named StuVoc1/StuVoc2/GK/ART3\" =\n      all(dim(Sigma_true) == 4) && setequal(colnames(Sigma_true), names(specs)),\n    \"`Sigma_true` must have a unit diagonal (it's a correlation matrix)\" =\n      isTRUE(all.equal(unname(diag(Sigma_true)), rep(1, 4), tolerance = 1e-6))\n  )\n  Sigma_true \u003c- Sigma_true[names(specs), names(specs)]\n\n  z \u003c- MASS::mvrnorm(n, mu = rep(0, 4), Sigma = Sigma_true)\n  colnames(z) \u003c- names(specs)\n\n  out \u003c- data.frame(id = seq_len(n))\n  for (t in names(specs)) {\n    sp  \u003c- specs[[t]]\n    cal \u003c- get_calibration(sp$mu, rel[[t]], sp$n_items, sp$guessing)\n    theta \u003c- cal$theta_mu + cal$theta_sigma * z[, t]\n    p \u003c- sp$guessing + (1 - sp$guessing) * plogis(theta)\n\n    if (identical(t, \"ART3\")) {\n      hits    \u003c- rbinom(n, sp$split[[\"authors\"]], p)\n      rejects \u003c- rbinom(n, sp$split[[\"foils\"]], p)\n      out$ART3          \u003c- hits + rejects\n      out$ART3_fn_rate  \u003c- 1 - hits / sp$split[[\"authors\"]]\n      out$ART3_fp_rate  \u003c- 1 - rejects / sp$split[[\"foils\"]]\n    } else {\n      out[[t]] \u003c- rbinom(n, sp$n_items, p)\n    }\n    if (keep_latent) {\n      out[[paste0(t, \"_theta\")]] \u003c- theta\n      out[[paste0(t, \"_p\")]]     \u003c- p\n    }\n  }\n  out\n}\n\n#' Simulate `n` participants on just *two* named tests, with a directly\n#' specified true (observed-score-scale) correlation and reliabilities.\n#' This is what the NHST/power/error-rate sweep engine below uses, rather\n#' than `simulate_battery()`'s full four-test matrix: powering/diagnosing a\n#' test only ever concerns one focal pair, and restricting the draw to\n#' that pair avoids needing the *other* two tests' correlations with the\n#' focal pair to stay mutually consistent (a full 4x4 correlation matrix\n#' stops being positive-definite surprisingly easily once one cell is\n#' pushed to an extreme value for a sweep, as the other cells were not\n#' built with that in mind).\n#'\n#' @param n           sample size.\n#' @param var_x, var_y  which two tests to simulate (must be among the\n#'                      four names in `default_test_specs()`).\n#' @param true_corr    target correlation between the two tests, on\n#'                      whichever scale `corr_scale` selects.\n#' @param corr_scale   `\"observed\"` (default): `true_corr` is the target\n#'                      *observed*-score correlation, and the function\n#'                      disattenuates internally to find the latent\n#'                      correlation that will produce it once measurement\n#'                      error is added -- use this for power/NHST work,\n#'                      where the population parameter being tested is the\n#'                      observed-score correlation. `\"latent\"`: `true_corr`\n#'                      is used directly as the correlation between the two\n#'                      tests' *true* abilities, with no compensation -- use\n#'                      this to demonstrate attenuation itself (holding the\n#'                      construct-level relationship fixed while varying\n#'                      reliability, so the *observed* correlation visibly\n#'                      drops as reliability drops).\n#' @param reliability_x, reliability_y  reliability for each test\n#'                      (defaults to each test's Vermeiren-default value).\n#' @param seed         for reproducibility.\n#' @return a data frame: `id`, and one score column per requested test\n#'   (plus `ART3_fp_rate`/`ART3_fn_rate` if `var_x`/`var_y` includes ART3).\nsimulate_pair \u003c- function(n, var_x, var_y, true_corr = 0, corr_scale = c(\"observed\", \"latent\"),\n                           reliability_x = NULL, reliability_y = NULL, seed = NULL) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  corr_scale \u003c- match.arg(corr_scale)\n  specs \u003c- default_test_specs()\n  stopifnot(\n    \"`var_x`/`var_y` must each be one of StuVoc1, StuVoc2, GK, ART3\" =\n      var_x %in% names(specs) && var_y %in% names(specs),\n    \"`var_x` and `var_y` must be different tests\" = var_x != var_y\n  )\n  rel_defaults \u003c- default_reliability_vec()\n  if (is.null(reliability_x)) reliability_x \u003c- unname(rel_defaults[[var_x]])\n  if (is.null(reliability_y)) reliability_y \u003c- unname(rel_defaults[[var_y]])\n\n  r_true \u003c- if (corr_scale == \"observed\") disattenuate(true_corr, reliability_x, reliability_y) else true_corr\n  Sigma \u003c- matrix(c(1, r_true, r_true, 1), nrow = 2)\n  z \u003c- MASS::mvrnorm(n, mu = c(0, 0), Sigma = Sigma)\n\n  out \u003c- data.frame(id = seq_len(n))\n  for (slot in list(list(name = var_x, z = z[, 1], rel = reliability_x),\n                     list(name = var_y, z = z[, 2], rel = reliability_y))) {\n    sp  \u003c- specs[[slot$name]]\n    cal \u003c- get_calibration(sp$mu, slot$rel, sp$n_items, sp$guessing)\n    theta \u003c- cal$theta_mu + cal$theta_sigma * slot$z\n    p \u003c- sp$guessing + (1 - sp$guessing) * plogis(theta)\n    if (identical(slot$name, \"ART3\")) {\n      hits    \u003c- rbinom(n, sp$split[[\"authors\"]], p)\n      rejects \u003c- rbinom(n, sp$split[[\"foils\"]], p)\n      out$ART3         \u003c- hits + rejects\n      out$ART3_fn_rate \u003c- 1 - hits / sp$split[[\"authors\"]]\n      out$ART3_fp_rate \u003c- 1 - rejects / sp$split[[\"foils\"]]\n    } else {\n      out[[slot$name]] \u003c- rbinom(n, sp$n_items, p)\n    }\n  }\n  out\n}\n\n#' Simulate `n_studies` independent studies of size `n`, for sampling-\n#' distribution work (distribution of a sample statistic across repeated\n#' studies). Returns one long data frame with a `study` id column, in the\n#' same spirit as sampling-distributions.R's simulate_studies().\nsimulate_studies_battery \u003c- function(n, n_studies, ..., seed = NULL) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  out \u003c- lapply(seq_len(n_studies), function(s) {\n    d \u003c- simulate_battery(n, ..., seed = NULL)\n    d$study \u003c- paste(\"Study\", s)\n    d\n  })\n  do.call(rbind, out)\n}\n\n# ---- NHST / diagnostic / sweep engine ---------------------------------------\n\n#' Run a two-sided Pearson correlation test between two tests' scores.\nfit_focal_cor \u003c- function(data, var_x, var_y) {\n  ct \u003c- stats::cor.test(data[[var_x]], data[[var_y]])\n  data.frame(estimate = unname(ct$estimate), ci_low = ct$conf.int[1],\n             ci_high = ct$conf.int[2], p_value = ct$p.value)\n}\n\n#' Classify one fitted test's result against the *true* value used to\n#' simulate the data: significant? (CI/p-value excludes zero at `alpha`),\n#' sign-correct? (only meaningful when true_value != 0 -- NA under the\n#' null, since there's no \"correct\" nonzero sign to match), CI coverage?\ndiagnose_cor_result \u003c- function(fit, true_value, alpha = 0.05) {\n  significant  \u003c- fit$p_value \u003c alpha\n  sign_correct \u003c- if (true_value == 0) NA else (sign(fit$estimate) == sign(true_value))\n  covers       \u003c- (true_value >= fit$ci_low) & (true_value \u003c= fit$ci_high)\n  data.frame(estimate = fit$estimate, p_value = fit$p_value,\n             significant = significant, sign_correct = sign_correct, covers = covers)\n}\n\n#' Sweep sample size, the focal pair's true (population) observed-score\n#' correlation, and (optionally) both focal tests' shared reliability,\n#' repeating `reps` independent simulated studies per grid cell. Revised core design: a parametric, sweep-friendly multi-test DGP\n\nThe user's stated aims require the DGP itself to be built for **sweeping**, not just\nfor reproducing one fixed battery. Concretely:\n\n1. Simulate participant-level **total accuracy scores** on each test (not just a\n   single score) — potentially thousands of simulated participants per run.\n2. **Simplifying assumption**: every simulated participant completes every test in the\n   battery (fully crossed, no missingness).\n3. Support generating **one study** (one dataset of N participants) or **many\n   studies** (repeated independent samples, varying N) from the same DGP.\n4. Three independently controllable DGP \"dials\", each a first-class function\n   argument (not hard-coded):\n   - (i) **participant sample size**, `n`\n   - (ii) **measurement error**, via a per-test **reliability** parameter\n   - (iii) **true (construct-level) correlation** between the latent abilities\n     underlying each pair of tests — i.e. the correlation the tests *would* show if\n     measured without error; the attenuation formula then determines how much lower\n     the *observed*-score correlation will be at a given reliability. This is itself\n     an important teaching point (measurement error attenuates observed\n     correlations), so the DGP must expose true-score correlation and reliability as\n     separate, independently variable inputs rather than only letting the user set\n     the observed-score correlation directly.\n5. This is the \"construct-level\"\nor disattenuated correlation structure. Vermeiren's Study-5 correlation matrix (Table\n8) is used as the **default** `Sigma_true`, but any entry (most importantly the\nStuVoc1–GK or StuVoc1–ART3 cell used as the focal pair in the NHST/power work) can be\noverridden — this is dial (iii).\n\n**Layer B — item-level measurement.** Each test's observed total score is built from\nsimulated item responses driven by that test's true ability, so scores stay\nrealistically bounded (0–50, 0–65, 0–90) rather than being continuous CTT scores, and\n\"total accuracy score\" is literal, not a stand-in. Two item-response mechanisms are\nneeded:\n\n- **4AFC accuracy items** (StuVoc1, StuVoc2, GK): `p_ij = 0.25 + 0.75 * plogis(a_t *\n  (theta_ti - b_j))` (guessing floor appropriate to 4 alternatives), responses\n  `~ Bernoulli(p_ij)`, summed to a bounded total score. Given the user's aims\n(sweeping sample size, reliability, and correlation independently; computing\nAims-1–2-style error-rate diagnostics across that sweep), the DGP instead:\n\n- Uses an explicit, overridable **correlation matrix** (not a fixed single `g`-factor\n  with hand-solved loadings) so arbitrary pairs of tests can have their true\n  correlation swept directly.\n- Treats **reliability as a true input parameter** per test/per sweep cell (via the\n  numeric discrimination solver), not a fixed, pre-calibrated constant — this is what\n  makes \"vary measurement error\" (dial ii) possible without re-deriving a new DGP for\n  every reliability value.\n- Keeps Vermeiren's numbers as sensible **defaults and a validation anchor** (Section\n  6), not as constraints baked into the simulator.\n\n## 4. <div><tool-result call-id="toolu_014zhQHWgmLi3dgMDEEToJoB"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 20.2KB, 434 lines, showing lines 1-80]\n1\t#' =======================================...[truncated, total 4380 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 20.2KB, 434 lines, showing lines 1-80]\n#' ============================================================\n#' sampling-distributions.R\n#'\n#' Simulates scores on a hypothetical 0-40 item vocabulary test from a\n#' trial level up, and draws the figure sequence: one dot -> two dots ->\n#' a \"pile of dots\" showing a sample's distribution -> a histogram -> a\n#' grid of histograms (repeated studies) -> a scatterplot against a\n#' continuous covariate.\n#'\n#' Model (trial level up, so every observed score is *structurally*\n#' bounded to [0, n_items] -- no post-hoc clipping is needed):\n#'\n#'   Ability (logit scale):  theta_i     ~ N(theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n#'   Per-item probability:   p_i         =  plogis(theta_i)\n#'   Trial-level responses:  Y_i1..Y_i40 ~  Bernoulli(p_i)   (independent)\n#'   Observed score:         score_i     =  sum_j Y_ij        in {0,...,40}\n#'\n#' `theta_mu` and `theta_sigma` aren't set directly -- they're solved\n#' numerically (see `calibrate_ability()`) so that the *emergent* mean\n#' score matches `mu`, and the emergent parallel-forms reliability\n#' (corr(score, score') for two independent administrations drawn from\n#' the same theta_i, i.e. the same person re-tested) matches\n#' `reliability`. This mirrors real test theory: for a fixed test\n#' length, how reliable a test is and how spread out scores are, are\n#' linked to each other and to the mean, not independently free knobs --\n#' fixing `mu` and one of {`reliability`, `sd_true`} determines the\n#' other. `calibrate_ability()` (and therefore `simulate_vocab_data()` /\n#' `simulate_parallel_forms()`) accepts either: pass `reliability` (the\n#' default) when a figure is about repeatability, or pass `sd_true`\n#' directly when a figure needs independent control of spread (e.g. two\n#' panels with the same mean but visibly different spread). Whichever\n#' one wasn't the calibration target is still available afterwards as an\n#' emergent value via `calibrate_ability()$moments`.\n#'\n#' `r_with_x` is specified on the *observed*-score scale, i.e. it's\n#' (approximately) the correlation you'll actually see in\n#' `plot_scatter()`. Because measurement error attenuates any\n#' correlation involving a noisy observed variable, hitting a target\n#' observed-score correlation requires a *larger* correlation between\n#' the underlying ability and x; classical test theory gives\n#' corr(observed, true ability) = sqrt(reliability), so that attenuation\n#' is inverted internally. If `r_with_x` exceeds what's achievable at\n#' the requested `reliability` (i.e. `abs(r_with_x) > sqrt(reliability)`),\n#' it's capped and a warning is issued.\n#'\n#' Requires: ggplot2, ggdist (for the dot-pile figure).\n#'\n#' Quarto usage:\n#'   ```{r}\n#'   source(\"sampling-distributions.R\")\n#'   d \u003c- simulate_vocab_data(n = 40, seed = 1)\n#'   plot_dots(d$observed_score[1])\n#'   plot_dots(d$observed_score[1:2])\n#'   plot_dotpile(d$observed_score)\n#'   plot_histogram(d$observed_score)\n#'   plot_histogram_grid(simulate_studies(6, 40, seed = 2))\n#'   plot_scatter(simulate_vocab_data(n = 60, r_with_x = 0.5, seed = 3))\n#'   ```\n#' ============================================================\n\nlibrary(ggplot2)\n\n# ---- calibration ------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' Expectation of `f(theta)` under theta ~ N(theta_mu, theta_sigma),\n#' via numerical integration (base R, no extra dependency).\nexpect_theta \u003c- function(f, theta_mu, theta_sigma) {\n  integrate(function(theta) f(theta) * dnorm(theta, theta_mu, theta_sigma),\n            lower = theta_mu - 10 * theta_sigma,\n            upper = theta_mu + 10 * theta_sigma)$value\n}\n\n#' Moments of the observed score implied by a given (theta_mu,\n#' theta_sigma, n_items), under the trial-level model described above.\n#' `var_error` uses the binomial variance n*p*(1-p) as the expected\n#' within-person sampling variance across the 40 items.\nimplied_moments \u003c- function(theta_mu, theta_sigma, n_items) {\n  p_bar  \u003c- expect_theta(plogis, theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n  p2_bar \u003c- expect_theta(function(th) plogis(th)^2, theta_mu, theta_sigma)\n  pq_bar \u003c- expect_theta(function(th) plogis(th) * (1 - plogis(th)), theta_mu, theta_sigma)"},"elapsedMs":7}</script></tool-result></div>

<div><tool-result call-id="toolu_01P1odwwgi6qve6d9sv53R6o"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 20.2KB, 434 lines, showing lines 230-433]\n230\t#'\n231\t#' @return a data frame: id, x...[truncated, total 9975 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 20.2KB, 434 lines, showing lines 230-433]\n#'\n#' @return a data frame: id, x, theta (ability, logit scale), p_correct\n#'   (per-item probability implied by theta), observed_score (integer,\n#'   always in [0, n_items] by construction).\nsimulate_vocab_data \u003c- function(n, mu = 30, reliability = 0.80, sd_true = NULL, r_with_x = 0,\n                                 x = NULL, x_mean = 0, x_sd = 1,\n                                 n_items = 40, seed = NULL) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  if (!is.null(sd_true) && !missing(reliability)) {\n    warning(paste(\n      \"Both `reliability` and `sd_true` were supplied to\",\n      \"simulate_vocab_data(); they aren't independently settable\",\n      \"(fixing mu and sd_true determines reliability, and vice versa).\",\n      \"Using `sd_true` and ignoring `reliability`.\"\n    ))\n  }\n  cal \u003c- calibrate_ability(mu, reliability = reliability, sd_true = sd_true, n_items = n_items)\n  reliability \u003c- cal$moments$reliability\n\n  if (is.null(x)) x \u003c- rnorm(n, x_mean, x_sd)\n\n  max_r \u003c- sqrt(reliability)\n  if (abs(r_with_x) > max_r) {\n    warning(sprintf(\n      paste(\"r_with_x = %.2f is not achievable at reliability = %.2f\",\n            \"(measurement error caps the observed-score correlation at\",\n            \"about %.2f); using %.2f instead.\"),\n      r_with_x, reliability, max_r, sign(r_with_x) * max_r\n    ))\n    r_with_x \u003c- sign(r_with_x) * max_r\n  }\n  if (r_with_x != 0 && n \u003c 2) {\n    warning(\"r_with_x is not meaningful for n \u003c 2 (correlation is undefined for a single observation); ignoring it.\")\n    r_with_x \u003c- 0\n  }\n  r_theta_x \u003c- if (r_with_x == 0) 0 else r_with_x / max_r\n\n  # Only standardise x (and only use it) when it's actually needed: with\n  # r_theta_x == 0, scale(x) may be NaN (e.g. n \u003c 2, or a constant x) and\n  # 0 * NaN is NaN in R, not 0 -- multiplying it in unconditionally would\n  # silently turn every theta (and hence every score) into NA.\n  z \u003c- rnorm(n)\n  if (r_theta_x == 0) {\n    theta_z \u003c- z\n  } else {\n    xz \u003c- as.numeric(scale(x))\n    if (anyNA(xz)) {\n      warning(\"x has zero variance (e.g. all identical values); r_with_x cannot be induced. Ignoring r_with_x.\")\n      theta_z \u003c- z\n    } else {\n      theta_z \u003c- r_theta_x * xz + sqrt(1 - r_theta_x^2) * z\n    }\n  }\n  theta \u003c- cal$theta_mu + cal$theta_sigma * theta_z\n  p_correct \u003c- plogis(theta)\n\n  observed_score \u003c- rbinom(n, size = n_items, prob = p_correct)\n\n  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), x = x, theta = theta, p_correct = p_correct,\n             observed_score = observed_score)\n}\n\n#' Simulate `n_studies` independent samples of size `n_per_study`, for\n#' the \"no two samples look identical\" histogram-grid figure.\n#' Returns one long data frame with a `study` id column.\nsimulate_studies \u003c- function(n_studies, n_per_study, seed = NULL, ...) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  out \u003c- lapply(seq_len(n_studies), function(s) {\n    d \u003c- simulate_vocab_data(n_per_study, seed = NULL, ...)\n    d$study \u003c- paste(\"Study\", s)\n    d\n  })\n  do.call(rbind, out)\n}\n\n#' Two independent administrations (parallel forms / test-retest) per\n#' person, sharing the same ability theta_i, to check/demonstrate the\n#' calibrated reliability directly (corr(form1, form2) ~ reliability).\n#' @param sd_true  alternate calibration target in place of `reliability`\n#'                  -- see `simulate_vocab_data()` / `calibrate_ability()`.\nsimulate_parallel_forms \u003c- function(n, mu = 30, reliability = 0.80, sd_true = NULL,\n                                     n_items = 40, seed = NULL) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  if (!is.null(sd_true) && !missing(reliability)) {\n    warning(paste(\n      \"Both `reliability` and `sd_true` were supplied to\",\n      \"simulate_parallel_forms(); they aren't independently settable.\",\n      \"Using `sd_true` and ignoring `reliability`.\"\n    ))\n  }\n  cal \u003c- calibrate_ability(mu, reliability = reliability, sd_true = sd_true, n_items = n_items)\n  theta \u003c- rnorm(n, cal$theta_mu, cal$theta_sigma)\n  p_correct \u003c- plogis(theta)\n  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), theta = theta, p_correct = p_correct,\n             form1 = rbinom(n, n_items, p_correct),\n             form2 = rbinom(n, n_items, p_correct))\n}\n\n# ---- figures ----------------------------------------------------------\n\n#' One or two scores plotted as points on a number line.\nplot_dots \u003c- function(scores, xlim = c(0, 40)) {\n  # y nudged just above 0 so the dot rests on top of the axis line\n  # rather than being bisected by it.\n  df \u003c- data.frame(score = scores, y = 0.04)\n  ggplot(df, aes(score, y)) +\n    geom_point(size = 6, color = \"#3B6EA5\") +\n    scale_x_continuous(name = \"Score (items correct)\") +\n    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.5), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +\n    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +\n    theme_minimal() +\n    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),\n          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),\n          axis.line.x = element_line(color = \"black\", linewidth = 0.9),\n          axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = \"black\"))\n}\n\n#' A sample's scores as a \"pile of dots\" (ggdist::stat_dots) -- shows\n#' the distribution as discrete points, not a smoothed density/histogram.\nplot_dotpile \u003c- function(scores, xlim = c(0, 40), ...) {\n  if (!requireNamespace(\"ggdist\", quietly = TRUE)) {\n    stop(\"Package 'ggdist' is required for plot_dotpile(). Install with install.packages('ggdist').\")\n  }\n  df \u003c- data.frame(score = scores)\n  ggplot(df, aes(x = score)) +\n    ggdist::stat_dots(color = \"#3B6EA5\", fill = \"#3B6EA5\", ...) +\n    scale_x_continuous(name = \"Score (items correct)\") +\n    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +\n    theme_minimal() +\n    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),\n          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),\n          axis.line.x = element_line(color = \"black\", linewidth = 0.9),\n          axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = \"black\"))\n}\n\n#' A grid of \"pile of dots\" distributions, one per \"study\" -- the\n#' ggdist::stat_dots analogue of plot_histogram_grid(), for showing\n#' sampling variability as discrete points rather than binned counts.\n#' @param data a data frame with a `study` and `observed_score` column,\n#'   e.g. from simulate_studies().\n#' @param binwidth dot diameter in data units (score points). ggdist's\n#'   default computes a separate binwidth per facet panel, sized to\n#'   stack that panel's tallest pile within the available height --\n#'   which makes dots different sizes across panels. Fixing binwidth\n#'   here keeps every panel's dots the same size.\nplot_dotpile_grid \u003c- function(data, value_col = \"observed_score\",\n                               xlim = c(0, 40), ncol = NULL, binwidth = 2.5, ...) {\n  if (!requireNamespace(\"ggdist\", quietly = TRUE)) {\n    stop(\"Package 'ggdist' is required for plot_dotpile_grid(). binwidth, ...) +\n    scale_x_continuous(name = \"Score (items correct)\") +\n    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +\n    facet_wrap(~study, ncol = ncol) +\n    theme_minimal() +\n    theme(axis.title.y = teaching contrast this script is built around, and the\n#' reason the two kinds of error get separate figures rather than one:\n#'\n#'   changing N changes the SPREAD of a statistic's sampling distribution\n#'   (plot_sampling_distribution());\n#'\n#'   changing reliability changes its CENTRE, via attenuation\n#'   (plot_attenuation_vs_reliability()), not (much) its spread --\n#'   these are different error sources with different fixes (a bigger N\n#'   does little to undo attenuation from an unreliable measure, and a\n#'   more reliable measure does little to narrow a sampling simulate_sampling_distribution()  -> plot_sampling_distribution()\n#'   simulate_attenuation_sweep()      -> plot_attenuation_vs_reliability()\n#'\n#' Requires: psych-battery-dgp.R sourced first (uses default_test_specs(),\n#' default_reliability_vec(), default_r_obs_matrix(), get_calibration(),\n#' simulate_pair(), disattenuate()); ggplot2; ggdist (for\n#' plot_sampling_distribution() only, same guarded-require pattern as\n#' sampling-distributions.R's plot_dotpile()).\n#'\n#' Quarto usage:\n#'   ```{r}\n#'   source(\"psych-battery-dgp.R\")\n#'   source(\"sampling-measurement-error.R\")\n#'\n#'   # measurement error: one test, one reliability\n#'   plot_true_vs_observed(\"StuVoc1\", n = 300, seed = 1)\n#'   plot_parallel_forms(\"StuVoc1\", n = statistic = \"cor\",\n#'                               var_x = \"StuVoc1\", var_y = \"GK\", seed = 3)\n#'\n#'   # measurement error again, now via attenuation of a correlation\n#'   plot_attenuation_vs_reliability(reliability_grid = seq(0.2, 0.95, by = 0.15),\n#'                                    n = 300, reps = 300,\n#'                                    var_x = \"StuVoc1\", var_y = \"GK\", seed = 4)\n#'   ```\n#' ============================================================\n\nlibrary(ggplot2)\n\n# ---- measurement error: one test, one person at a time ---------------------\n\n#' Simulate `n` participants on a single test from the battery, keeping\n#' each person's standardized true ability (`true_ability`, z-scale) --\n#' the single-test building block behind plot_true_vs_observed().\n#'\n#' @param test         one of \"StuVoc1\", \"StuVoc2\", \"GK\", \"ART3\".\n#' @param n            number of simulated participants.\n#' @param reliability  this test's reliability (dial ii); NULL (default)\n#'                      uses its Vermeiren-default value.\n#' @param seed         for reproducibility.\n#' @return a data frame: `id`, `test`, `true_ability` (standardized,\n#'   mean 0 / sd 1), `theta` (ability, logit scale), `p` (per-item/\n#'   per-name probability implied by theta), `score`, `n_items` (test\n#'   length score is bounded by), `reliability` (the value actually\n#'   used).\nsimulate_single_test \u003c- function(test = \"StuVoc1\", n = 500, reliability = NULL, seed = NULL) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  specs \u003c- default_test_specs()\n  stopifnot(\n    \"`test` must be one of StuVoc1, StuVoc2, GK, ART3\" = test %in% names(specs),\n    \"`n` must be a positive integer\" = n >= 1\n  )\n  rel \u003c- if (is.null(reliability)) unname(default_reliability_vec()[[test]]) else reliability\n  stopifnot(\"`reliability` must be strictly between 0 and 1\" = rel > 0 && rel \u003c 1)\n\n  sp  \u003c- specs[[test]]\n  cal \u003c- get_calibration(sp$mu, rel, sp$n_items, sp$guessing)\n  z     \u003c- rnorm(n)\n  theta \u003c- cal$theta_mu + cal$theta_sigma * z\n  p     \u003c- sp$guessing + (1 - \u003c- hits + rejects\n    n_items  \u003c- sum(sp$split)\n  } else {\n    score    \u003c- rbinom(n, sp$n_items, p)\n    n_items  \u003c- sp$n_items\n  }\n\n  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), test = test, true_ability = z, theta = theta, p = p,\n             score = score, n_items = n_items, reliability = rel)\n}\n\n#' A person's observed score plotted against their (otherwise\n#' unobservable) true ability -- the single clearest picture of\n#' measurement error: vertical scatter of points around the expected-\n#' score curve is score variation that has nothing to do with sample\n#' size, only with how few items/names the test has to work with.\n#'\n#' @inheritParams simulate_single_test\n#' @return a ggplot object.\nplot_true_vs_observed \u003c- function(test = \"StuVoc1\", n = 300, reliability = NULL, seed = NULL) {\n  d   \u003c- simulate_single_test(test, n, reliability, seed)\n  sp  \u003c- default_test_specs()[[test]]\n  rel \u003c- d$reliability[1]\n  cal \u003c- get_calibration(sp$mu, rel, sp$n_items, sp$guessing)\n\n  z_grid     \u003c- seq(-3.2, 3.2, length.out = 200)\n  theta_grid \u003c- cal$theta_mu + cal$theta_sigma * z_grid\n  p_grid     \u003c- sp$guessing + (1 - sp$guessing) * plogis(theta_grid)\n  curve_df   \u003c- data.frame(true_ability = z_grid, expected_score = d$n_items[1] * p_grid)\n\n  ggplot(d, aes(true_ability, score)) +\n    geom_point(color = \"#3B6EA5\", alpha = 0.6) +\n    geom_line(data = curve_df, aes(true_ability, expected_score), color = \"#B23A48\", linewidth = 1) +\n    labs(x = \"True ability (standardized)\", y = sprintf(\"%s score\", test),\n         subtitle = sprintf(\n           \"reliability = %.2f \\u2014 vertical scatter around the red curve is measurement error\",\n           rel)) +\n    theme_minimal()\n}\n\n#' Two independent \"administrations\" of the same test to the same `n`\n#' simulated people (sharing the same true ability, independent item\n#' draws) -- the parallel-forms/test-retest check used throughout this\n#' project (same device as sampling-distributions.R's\n#' simulate_parallel_forms()), generalized across all four battery\n#' tests.\n#'\n#' @inheritParams simulate_single_test\n#' @return a data frame: `id`, `test`, `true_ability`, `form1`, `form2`\n#'   (two independently simulated scores per person), `reliability`.\nsimulate_parallel_forms_battery \u003c- function(test = \"StuVoc1\", n = 500, reliability = NULL, seed = NULL) {\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  specs \u003c- default_test_specs()\n  stopifnot(\"`test` must be one of StuVoc1, StuVoc2, GK, ART3\" = test %in% names(specs))\n  rel \u003c- if (is.null(reliability)) unname(default_reliability_vec()[[test]]) else reliability\n  stopifnot(\"`reliability` must be strictly between 0 and 1\" = rel > 0 && rel \u003c 1)\n\n  sp  \u003c- specs[[test]]\n  cal \u003c- get_calibration(sp$mu, rel, sp$n_items, sp$guessing)\n  z     \u003c- rnorm(n)\n  theta \u003c- cal$theta_mu + cal$theta_sigma * z\n  p     \u003c- sp$guessing + (1 - sp$guessing) * plogis(theta)\n\n  draw_once \u003c- function() {\n    if (identical(test, \"ART3\")) {\n      rbinom(n, sp$split[[\"authors\"]], p) + rbinom(n, sp$split[[\"foils\"]], p)\n    } else {\n      rbinom(n, sp$n_items, p)\n    }\n  }\n  data.frame(id = seq_len(n), test = test, true_ability = z,\n             form1 = draw_once(), form2 = draw_once(), reliability = rel)\n}\n\n#' Scatterplot of one test's two parallel-form scores, with the\n#' observed correlation annotated against its reliability target --\n#' reliability *is* parallel-forms correlation in this model.\n#'\n#' @inheritParams simulate_single_test\n#' @return a ggplot object.\nplot_parallel_forms \u003c- function(test = \"StuVoc1\", n = 300, reliability = NULL, seed = NULL) {\n  d     \u003c- simulate_parallel_forms_battery(test, n, reliability, seed)\n  r_obs \u003c- cor(d$form1, d$form2)\n\n  ggplot(d, aes(form1, form2)) +\n    geom_point(color = \"#3B6EA5\", alpha = 0.6) +\n    geom_smooth(method = \"lm\", se = TRUE, color = \"#B23A48\") +\n    coord_equal() +\n    labs(x = \"Form 1 score\", y = \"Form 2 score\",\n         subtitle = sprintf(\"%s \\u2014 target reliability = %.2f, observed r(form1, form2) = %.2f\",\n `n`, each\n#' contributing one value of a chosen summary statistic -- the building\n#' block for a sampling distribution.\n#'\n#' @param n            participants per study (dial i).\n#' @param n_studies    number of independent studies to simulate.\n#' @param statistic    `\"mean\"` (mean score on `var_x`) or `\"cor\"`\n#'                      (Pearson correlation between `var_x` and\n#' population *observed*-score correlation to\n#'                      simulate from, for `statistic = \"cor\"`; NULL\n#'                      (default) uses the Vermeiren-default value for\n#' least 2 to show a distribution\" = n_studies >= 2\n  )\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  rel_default \u003c- default_reliability_vec()\n  rel_x \u003c- if (is.null(reliability)) \"observed\",\n                          reliability_x = rel_x, reliability_y = rel_y, seed = NULL)\n      cor(d[[var_x]], d[[var_y]])\n    }, numeric(1))\n  }\n  data.frame(study = seq_len(n_studies), n = n, statistic = statistic, value = values)\n}\n\n#' A \"pile of dots\" (ggdist::stat_dots, as in sampling-distributions.R)\n#' for the sampling distribution of a chosen statistic, one panel per\n#' sample size in `n_grid` -- the sampling-error figure: panels narrow\n#' (spread shrinks) as N grows from top to bottom, but stay centred in\n#' the same place.\n#'\n#' @inheritParams simulate_sampling_distribution\n#' @param n_grid    sample sizes to compare, one facet panel each.\n#' @param n_studies independent studies simulated *per* panel.\n#' @return a ggplot object.\nplot_sampling_distribution \u003c- function(n_grid, n_studies = 300, statistic = c(\"mean\", \"cor\"),\n                                        var_x = \"StuVoc1\", var_y = NULL,\n                                        reliability = NULL, true_corr = NULL, seed = NULL) {\n  statistic \u003c- match.arg(statistic)\n  if (!requireNamespace(\"ggdist\", quietly = TRUE)) {\n    stop(\"Package 'ggdist' is required for plot_sampling_distribution(). Install with install.packages('ggdist').\")\n  }\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  combined \u003c- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_grid, function(n) {\n    simulate_sampling_distribution(n, n_studies, statistic, var_x, var_y, reliability, true_corr, seed = NULL)\n  }))\n  n_levels \u003c- sort(unique(combined$n))\n  combined$n_label \u003c- factor(combined$n, levels = n_levels, labels = paste(\"n =\", n_levels))\n  xlab \u003c- if (statistic == \"mean\") sprintf(\"Sample mean (%s)\", var_x) else sprintf(\"Sample correlation, r(%s, %s)\", var_x, var_y)\n\n  ggplot(combined, aes(x = value)) +\n    ggdist::stat_dots(color = \"#3B6EA5\", fill = \"#3B6EA5\") +\n    facet_wrap(~n_label, ncol = 1) +\n    labs(x = xlab,\n         subtitle = \"Each dot is one simulated study's estimate \\u2014 larger N narrows the spread (sampling error), not the centre\") +\n    theme_minimal() +\n    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),\n          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = \"bold\"))\n}\n\n# ---- measurement error again: attenuation of a correlation ------------------\n\n#' Hold the *construct-level* (true-score) correlation between two\n#' tests fixed, and vary their (shared) reliability -- shows the\n#' observed-score correlation shrinking toward zero as reliability\n#' drops, purely from measurement error, with sample size untouched.\n#'\n#' @param reliability_grid  reliability values to sweep (applied to\n#'                           both `var_x` and `var_y` equally).\n#' @param n                 participants per simulated study (held\n#'                           fixed across the sweep).\n#' @param reps              independent studies simulated per\n#'                           reliability value.\n#' @param var_x, var_y      the focal pair of tests.\n#' @param true_corr_latent  the *true* (disattenuated) correlation to\n#'                           hold fixed; NULL (default) backs it out\n#'                           from the Vermeiren-default *observed*\n#'                           correlation and reliabilities for this\n#'                           pair, via disattenuate().\n#' @param seed              for reproducibility.\n#' @return a data frame: `reliability`, `rep`, `r_observed`, with the\n#'   fixed `true_corr_latent` value attached as an attribute.\nsimulate_attenuation_sweep \u003c- function(reliability_grid, n = 300, reps = 200,\n                                        var_x = \"StuVoc1\", var_y = \"GK\",\n                                        true_corr_latent = NULL, seed = NULL) {\n  stopifnot(\n    \"`var_x` and `var_y` must be different tests\" = var_x != var_y,\n    \"`reliability_grid` values must all be strictly between 0 and 1\" =\n      all(reliability_grid > 0 & reliability_grid \u003c 1),\n    \"`reps` must be at least 2\" = reps >= 2\n  )\n  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)\n  if (is.null(true_corr_latent)) {\n    rel_default      \u003c- default_reliability_vec()\n    r_obs_default    \u003c- default_r_obs_matrix()[var_x, var_y]\n    true_corr_latent \u003c- disattenuate(r_obs_default, rel_default[[var_x]], rel_default[[var_y]])\n  }\n  grid \u003c- expand.grid(reliability = reliability_grid, rep = seq_len(reps))\n  grid$r_observed \u003c- mapply(function(rel, rp) {\n    d \u003c- simulate_pair(n, var_x, var_y, true_corr = true_corr_latent, corr_scale = \"latent\",\n                        reliability_x = rel, reliability_y = rel, seed = NULL)\n    cor(d[[var_x]], d[[var_y]])\n  }, grid$reliability, grid$rep)\n  attr(grid, \"true_corr_latent\") \u003c- true_corr_latent\n  grid\n}\n\n#' The attenuation figure: observed r (y) against reliability (x), with\n#' a ribbon showing the empirical spread across `reps` studies, the\n#' theoretical attenuation line `r_obs = r_true * reliability`, and a\n#' dotted reference line at the fixed true (construct-level)\n#' correlation -- the ceiling you'd see with perfectly reliable\n#' measurement.\n#'\n#' @inheritParams simulate_attenuation_sweep\n#' @return a ggplot object.\nplot_attenuation_vs_reliability \u003c- function(reliability_grid, n = 300, reps = 200,\n                                             var_x = \"StuVoc1\", var_y = \"GK\",\n                                             true_corr_latent = NULL, seed = NULL) {\n  raw \u003c- simulate_attenuation_sweep(reliability_grid, n, reps, var_x, var_y, true_corr_latent, seed)\n  tc  \u003c- attr(raw, \"true_corr_latent\")\n\n  summ_list \u003c- lapply(split(raw$r_observed, raw$reliability), function(v) {\n    data.frame(mean = mean(v), lo = unname(quantile(v, .025)), hi = unname(quantile(v, .975)))\n  })\n  summ_df \u003c- do.call(rbind, summ_list)\n  summ_df$reliability \u003c- as.numeric(names(summ_list))\n  summ_df \u003c- summ_df[order(summ_df$reliability), ]\n\n  curve_df \u003c- data.frame(reliability = sort(unique(raw$reliability)))\n  curve_df$theory \u003c- tc * curve_df$reliability\n\n  ggplot(summ_df, aes(reliability, mean)) +\n    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = \"#3B6EA5\", alpha = 0.2) +\n    geom_line(color = \"#3B6EA5\", linewidth = 1) +\n    geom_point(color = \"#3B6EA5\", size = 2) +\n    geom_line(data = curve_df, aes(reliability, theory), color = \"#B23A48\", linetype = \"dashed\") +\n    geom_hline(yintercept = tc, color = \"gray40\", linetype = \"dotted\") +\n    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +\n    labs(x = \"Reliability (both tests, held equal)\",\n         y = sprintf(\"Observed r(%s, %s)\", var_x, var_y),\n         subtitle = sprintf(\n           paste(\"True (construct-level) correlation held fixed at %.2f (dotted line);\",\n                 \"dashed line = attenuation formula, r_obs = r_true \\u00d7 reliability\"),\n           tc)) +\n    theme_minimal()\n}\n","language":"r"}}</script></tool-call></div>
